items.title: PolicyStack
items.text:
PolicyStack manages OpenShift cluster configuration as Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management (ACM) policies kept in Git. Each directory under stack/ is an element, a Helm chart that renders policies through the policy-library chart. On the ACM hub, an Argo CD ApplicationSet creates one Application per element for every managed cluster that has a fleet file, which pins the cluster to a Git revision. Argo CD renders each Application at that revision and syncs it to the hub only. ACM delivers each policy to the single cluster it targets, where the governance add-on enforces it or reports compliance.

A fleet file that names a hub in hub also makes that hub build the cluster, with HyperShift, Hive or SiteConfig, and destroy it on state: absent (Cluster lifecycle).

items.title: How a change reaches a cluster
items.text:
1. Change an element, the root values.yaml or a file under values/ on the branch or tag that the cluster's fleet file pins. Clusters pinned to other revisions are unaffected. A change to the fleet file itself counts only on the default branch.
  2. Argo CD renders the element chart with the cluster's values cascade and syncs the Policy, PolicySet, Placement and PlacementBinding objects into the policy namespace on the hub.
  3. The Placement selects only that cluster. ACM replicates each Policy into the cluster's namespace on the hub, and the governance add-on on the managed cluster applies it. enforce changes the cluster, inform only reports. Compliance status returns to the replicated Policy on the hub.

items.title: Terms
items.text: Term Meaning Element A directory under stack/ holding a Helm chart that depends on the policy-library chart. Its values define the policies it renders. Fleet file A file on the repo's default branch that declares one cluster: fleet/<cluster>.yaml, or fleet/hubs/<hubName>.yaml for a hub. It sets the cluster's revision and the values files it reads, and optionally the hub that builds the cluster. Hub The cluster that runs ACM and OpenShift GitOps. It runs the ApplicationSets and holds the Applications and Policies, and the control planes of the clusters it builds. By default ACM also manages the hub as local-cluster, so it can have a fleet file like any other managed cluster, at fleet/hubs/<hubName>.yaml (The hub). Managed cluster A cluster that ACM manages and the GitOpsCluster imports into Argo CD, either imported by hand or built by a hub (Cluster lifecycle). It gets one Application per element once it has a fleet file. Release The Application name, which Argo CD also uses as the Helm release name. <element>-<cluster>, or <element>-<hubName> on the hub. Policy, PolicySet, Placement and PlacementBinding names are built from it. Revision The Git branch, tag or SHA in a cluster's fleet file. All of that cluster's Applications render from it. Values cascade The values files Argo CD passes to Helm for one Application, most of them listed in valueFiles in the cluster's fleet file. Later files override earlier ones.

items.title: Clusters and Applications
items.text:
The ApplicationSet policystack in openshift-gitops on the hub creates one Argo CD Application per element for every managed cluster that has a fleet file. The fleet file picks the Git revision and the values files. The template is install/templates/appset.yaml.

A second ApplicationSet, policystack-lifecycle, creates one Application per fleet file that names this hub in hub, or a managed hub it builds for (Global Hub). That Application builds or destroys the cluster (Cluster lifecycle). Its template is install/templates/lifecycle.yaml.

items.title: Fleet files
items.text:
A fleet file declares one cluster. A managed cluster's file is fleet/<cluster>.yaml, named exactly like its ManagedCluster. The hub's file is fleet/hubs/<hubName>.yaml (The hub).

Key Required Effect revision Yes Branch, tag or commit SHA every Application for the cluster renders from (Revision). valueFiles No Paths under values/, lowest precedence first. Each entry adds that file to the cascade (Order). hub No hubName of the hub that builds the cluster. Without it the cluster must be imported (Cluster lifecycle). state No present (default) or absent. absent destroys the cluster (Destroy). Requires hub. install No The cluster to build (Fleet keys). Requires hub. version No OpenShift release, x.y.z, the cluster runs. Bumping it upgrades the cluster (Upgrades). Required with hub. channel No Upgrade channel, such as stable-4.20 (Upgrades).

No other keys are allowed. A hub's own file cannot set hub, state or install, and hub must name a hub that has a file in fleet/hubs/. The Day-2 ApplicationSet ignores the three lifecycle keys. version and channel go only in the fleet file, never in a values layer, so the clusters an upgrade moves are the fleet files it changes. Argo CD reads fleet files as YAML 1.1, so revision, version and channel must be YAML strings. Quote one YAML reads as a number or a boolean: "1.10", "20261003", "on". Unquoted, revision: 1.10 pins 1.1. The validator checks these rules and that every valueFiles entry is a file (Validation).

# fleet/prod-east-1.yaml
revision: main
valueFiles:
  - environments/prod.yaml
  - datacenters/dc1.yaml
  - platforms/aws.yaml

Any file under values/ can be listed. tenants/payments.yaml is a custom layer: add the file and list it where it should rank. An old config.<baseDomain>/<category>.<priority>: <value> label becomes the entry <category>s/<value>.yaml, placed in priority order.

Upstream ships no live fleet files, since a shipped file would configure a real cluster as soon as someone installs from upstream. The examples are the validator's fixtures in tools/validator/testdata/clusters/: prod-east-1.yaml, nonprod-west-1.yaml, hubs/acm-dc1.yaml, and the hub-built hcp-kubevirt.yaml, hcp-agent.yaml, hcp-retired.yaml, hive-aws.yaml, hive-retired.yaml, sno-edge.yaml and sno-retired.yaml.

The ApplicationSet reads fleet files only from the repo's default branch, as HEAD. Copies of fleet/ on other branches have no effect. Changing the default branch re-points every cluster to the fleet files on the new branch, and a cluster without one there loses its Applications.

Fleet changes reach Argo CD within about 6 minutes: the ApplicationSet controller re-runs its generators every 3 minutes, and Argo CD caches the commit a branch points to for 3 minutes. An ApplicationSet webhook makes changes immediate, except the fix for a failed generation, which still waits for the 3 minute retry.

PolicyStack still reads five labels. ACM sets the first four, and nobody sets them by hand:

Label Set by Effect clusterID ACM, on OpenShift clusters Selects the cluster's Argo CD secret and becomes selectedId. A cluster without it gets no Applications. local-cluster ACM, on the hub Switches the cluster to the hub's fleet file and names it by hubName (The hub). name ACM The ManagedCluster name. The Placement selector matches on it (Placement). apps.open-cluster-management.io/cluster-name ACM's GitOpsCluster, on the cluster secret Matches a fleet file's hub to a default-mode managed hub (Lifecycle generator). global-hub.open-cluster-management.io/deploy-mode You, when importing a managed hub into a Global Hub default switches the managed hub to its hub file, fleet/hubs/<cluster>.yaml, and lets this hub build its clusters (Global Hub).

items.title: Revision
items.text:
revision is a branch, a tag or a commit SHA. Branch names with / work.

If a fleet file this hub reads does not parse, has no revision, or pins a revision that does not exist, ApplicationSet generation fails. Argo CD then creates, updates and deletes no Applications for any cluster until the file is fixed. The ApplicationSet's ErrorOccurred condition holds the error:

oc get applicationset policystack -n openshift-gitops \
  -o jsonpath='{.status.conditions[?(@.type=="ErrorOccurred")].message}'

A fleet file that does not parse stops policystack-lifecycle the same way, so the hub creates, upgrades and destroys no cluster until it is fixed. A bad revision there breaks only that cluster's lifecycle-<cluster> Application. Check it with the same command on policystack-lifecycle.

Pin tags, commit SHAs, protected branches, or a branch you keep until its pin moves off. A pinned branch that is deleted freezes the whole fleet, and GitHub deletes a pull request's branch on merge when automatic deletion of head branches is on.

The generator reads HEAD rather than main, so it follows a rename of the default branch.

The Render Diff comment on a PR shows each cluster's Policies at its revision before and after the merge.

items.title: The hub
items.text:
The hub's own ManagedCluster carries ACM's local-cluster label. Its fleet file is fleet/hubs/<hubName>.yaml, where hubName is an install chart value set once per hub, with no default (The install chart). A Global Hub managed hub imported in default mode has no local-cluster, so the global hub reads its file for it (Global Hub).

# fleet/hubs/acm-dc1.yaml
revision: main
valueFiles:
  - environments/prod.yaml
  - datacenters/dc1.yaml
  - platforms/baremetal.yaml
  - acm/acm-dc1.yaml

On the hub, hubName replaces the ManagedCluster name everywhere: the Applications are <element>-<hubName>, the cluster values file is values/clusters/<hubName>.yaml, and selectedName is hubName. Changing hubName renames the hub's Applications and every object they render. Hubs in the same datacenter share files such as acm/acm-dc1.yaml by listing them.

hubName is a chart value because nothing on the hub gives it a stable, unique name:

  • Every hub's own ManagedCluster is named local-cluster by default, so the cluster name cannot tell two hubs reading this repo apart.
  • ACM's localClusterName (ACM 2.14 and later) changes only at install, or after turning off hub self-management.
  • OpenShift's clusterID is a UUID that changes when a hub is rebuilt.

So each hub's identity is set once in its install release, and its configuration stays in Git. helm get values policystack -n openshift-gitops shows a hub's hubName. hubs/ is a subdirectory so a hub's file cannot collide with a managed cluster of the same name.

Every hub reading the same repo, including a passive or disaster recovery hub, sets its own hubName at helm install (Install PolicyStack). The chart fails without it, rather than apply another hub's configuration. Upgrades reuse the stored value.

items.title: Protection
items.text:
PolicyStack reads no other labels. Short of editing the five labels above, which RBAC on ManagedClusters and on Secrets in openshift-gitops guards, oc label cannot change what a cluster runs. Whoever can merge to fleet/ on the default branch decides it instead. The repo ships no CODEOWNERS file, because owners differ per fork. Add:

  • A CODEOWNERS entry for /fleet/.
  • A ruleset on the default branch that requires a pull request with code owner review, and blocks force pushes and deletion.
# .github/CODEOWNERS
/fleet/ @<org>/<team>

To require code owner review only for production clusters, own /fleet/prod-*.yaml and /fleet/hubs/ instead of /fleet/.

The same review guards cluster creation and destruction: a merged state: absent destroys the cluster (Destroy).

items.title: Generators
items.text:
The generator, as rendered with hubName=acm-dc1:

generators:
  - matrix:
      generators:
        - matrix:
            generators:
              - clusters:
                  selector:
                    matchExpressions:
                      - key: clusterID
                        operator: Exists
              - git:
                  repoURL: 'https://github.com/PolicyStack/PolicyStack.git'
                  revision: HEAD
                  pathParamPrefix: fleet
                  files:
                  - path: 'fleet/{{if index .metadata.labels "local-cluster"}}hubs/acm-dc1{{else if eq (index .metadata.labels "global-hub.open-cluster-management.io/deploy-mode") "default"}}hubs/{{.name}}{{else}}{{.name}}{{end}}.yaml'
        - git:
            repoURL: 'https://github.com/PolicyStack/PolicyStack.git'
            revision: '{{.revision}}'
            directories:
            - path: 'stack/*'
  1. A clusters generator. Every Argo CD cluster secret with a clusterID label.
  2. A git files generator. The cluster's fleet file at HEAD, fleet/hubs/<hubName>.yaml on a cluster labeled local-cluster, fleet/hubs/<cluster>.yaml on a managed hub labeled deploy-mode=default, and fleet/<cluster>.yaml otherwise. The file's keys become parameters. pathParamPrefix: fleet moves the file's path parameters under fleet, because a matrix keeps the first child's value when two children set the same parameter, and the file's path would otherwise replace the directory's.
  3. A git directories generator. Every directory under stack/ in gitRepo, at the fleet file's revision.

The inner matrix pairs each cluster with its fleet file. A cluster without one pairs with nothing. The outer matrix pairs each cluster with the directories, and each cluster and directory pair becomes one Application. The directory list comes from the cluster's own revision, so an element added on one branch reaches only clusters on a revision that contains it. Every directory gets an Application whether the element is enabled or not. A disabled element renders no objects.

The GitOpsCluster from Install PolicyStack creates one cluster secret per managed cluster. Clusters without a fleet file are imported but get no Applications.

items.title: Lifecycle generator
items.text:
policystack-lifecycle has two generators, as rendered with hubName=acm-dc1:

generators:
  - matrix:
      generators:
        - clusters:
            selector:
              matchExpressions:
                - key: local-cluster
                  operator: Exists
        - git: &fleet
            repoURL: 'https://github.com/PolicyStack/PolicyStack.git'
            revision: HEAD
            files:
            - path: 'fleet/*.yaml'
            - path: 'fleet/*/*.yaml'
              exclude: true
          selector:
            matchExpressions:
              - key: hub
                operator: In
                values:
                  - "acm-dc1"
  - matrix:
      generators:
        - git: *fleet
          selector:
            matchExpressions:
              - key: hub
                operator: Exists
        - clusters:
            selector:
              matchLabels:
                apps.open-cluster-management.io/cluster-name: '{{ if regexMatch "^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$" (toString .hub) }}{{ .hub }}{{ end }}'
                global-hub.open-cluster-management.io/deploy-mode: default

Both read every fleet file at HEAD. Argo CD's default globbing lets * match /, so fleet/*.yaml also matches files in subdirectories, and the exclude entry drops them: the hub files and anything else under a subdirectory, which neither ApplicationSet nor the validator reads. A file without hub never matches, so imported clusters get no lifecycle Application.

  1. The hub's own clusters. The selector keeps files whose hub is this hub's hubName, paired with the hub's own cluster secret. A hub that does not manage itself has none and builds nothing.
  2. Clusters of default-mode managed hubs (Global Hub). Each file with hub is paired with the cluster secret of the ManagedCluster it names, if that cluster is a managed hub imported in default mode. The fleet files come first because Argo CD templates a child generator's fields but not its selector. A hub that is not a DNS label matches nothing, since as a label value it would fail the whole ApplicationSet.

The cluster secret supplies .name, the ManagedCluster the Policies are placed on.

items.title: Applications
items.text:
Field Value Name <element>-<cluster>, or <element>-<hubName> on a cluster labeled local-cluster Project default Source stack/<element> in gitRepo at the cluster's revision, rendered by Helm with the values cascade Destination The hub, https://kubernetes.default.svc, namespace open-cluster-management Sync Automated with prune, selfHeal and allowEmpty, sync option RespectIgnoreDifferences=true

<element> is the directory name and <cluster> the ManagedCluster name. Argo CD uses the Application name as the Helm release name, and every rendered object name derives from it (Rendered objects, Naming limits).

Argo CD deploys only to the hub. ACM delivers the policies to the managed clusters (Placement). The chart sets policyNamespace on every object it renders, so the destination namespace is unused.

allowEmpty lets automated sync prune a disabled element down to no objects (Disabling an element).

policystack sets preserveResourcesOnDeletion: false, so its Applications carry the resources finalizer and deleting one deletes its objects on the hub (Removing an element). Removal stays bounded:

  • A failed render prunes nothing. The Application reports a ComparisonError and keeps its objects.
  • A failed generation deletes nothing. The ApplicationSet changes no Application until it is fixed (Revision).
  • The destination is always the hub, so Argo CD deletes only hub objects. ACM then removes the policies from the managed cluster (What happens on the managed cluster).

ACM copies each Policy into the cluster's namespace on the hub. From policy-library 3.1.0 the chart sets copyPolicyMetadata: false, so the copies carry no Argo CD tracking labels or annotations, and Argo CD never prunes them. Clusters pinned to a revision with an older chart pin still copy the metadata until their pin moves.

The lifecycle Applications differ:

Field Value Name lifecycle-<cluster>, where <cluster> is the fleet file name Source lifecycle/ in gitRepo at the fleet file's revision, with the same cascade (Order) Destination The hub, namespace open-cluster-management Sync Automated with prune and selfHeal

policystack-lifecycle also sets preserveResourcesOnDeletion: false. Deleting a lifecycle Application deletes its Policies, and the cluster keeps running unmanaged (Abandon).

items.title: Injected values
items.text:
Each Application passes these keys to Helm in valuesObject, built from the cluster's ACM labels and hubName. Order gives their precedence over the values files.

Key Value selectedName The cluster name, or hubName on the hub. selectedId The clusterID label. selector.matchExpressions A map with one In expression on the name label, under the key name. version, channel The fleet file's keys, only when it sets them.

Elements can read every key. The policy-library chart turns selector into each Placement's cluster selector (Placement). On the hub, selectedName is hubName, but the name expression holds the hub's ManagedCluster name. An element that needs a fact such as the environment reads a key that the matching values file sets. For prod-east-1:

selectedName: prod-east-1
selectedId: <clusterID>
selector:
  matchExpressions:
    name:
      key: name
      operator: In
      values:
        - "prod-east-1"

A lifecycle Application passes selector.matchExpressions.hub, one In expression on the name label holding the name of the hub's ManagedCluster the Policies apply to, and the fleet file's own keys: hub, state (default present), version and channel when set, and install (default {}). They rank above every values file, so the fleet file's install overrides the cascade (Values).

items.title: The install chart
items.text:
The install chart installs both ApplicationSets, the cluster import into Argo CD and its RBAC (Install PolicyStack). Its values:

Value Set in Use gitRepo --set at helm install The repository the git generators read and every Application renders from. Required. hubName --set at helm install Names this hub's fleet file, fleet/hubs/<hubName>.yaml, its Applications and its cluster values file. Selects the fleet files whose hub this hub builds. Unused on a default-mode Global Hub managed hub (Global Hub). Required (The hub). policyNamespace install/values.yaml The namespace the chart creates. Elements read the same value from the root values.yaml, and CI checks the two match. Do not change it.

helm upgrade --reset-then-reuse-values keeps gitRepo and hubName. To see the ApplicationSets as Argo CD gets them:

helm template policystack ./install --set hubName=acm-dc1 --set gitRepo=https://github.com/PolicyStack/PolicyStack.git

items.title: Writing an element
items.text:
An element is a Helm chart under stack/ that renders ACM policies through the policy-library chart.

Name it in lowercase kebab-case and keep the directory name and chart name identical. The Application, and so the Helm release, takes the directory name (Applications). The values key comes from the chart name. element: dependencies and the validator assume the two match.

Keep the name short: use the product's common abbreviation (acm, odf) or a plain noun (logging), without an openshift- prefix or -operator suffix. The name must not start with another element's name followed by -, since gitops on cluster dev-c and gitops-dev on cluster c would both be release gitops-dev-c (POLICY091). lifecycle is reserved. Element and policy names are part of every object name, so renaming one recreates its Policies on every cluster.

items.title: Creating an element
items.text:
From the repo root:

./tools/create-element.sh <name> "<description>"

It prompts for whatever is not given, then copies tools/sample-element/ to stack/<name>/, replacing my-element with the name and myElement with its camelCase form (cert-manager reads stack.certManager). It refuses a name that is not lowercase kebab-case or already exists. The result passes the validator as is.

The sample is the metallb pattern cut to one of each piece: an operator under an install policy, a config policy that depends on it, a toggle, and one converter that reads config. Policies start in inform. Then:

  1. Set the operator's namespace, operatorGroup and subscription in values.yaml.
  2. Replace converters/<name>-configmap.yaml with one file per templateNames entry. The validator fails on a missing converter (POLICY020) and warns on an unused one (POLICY021).
  3. Describe each setting with # @desc: and generate the README (Element reference).
  4. Run the validator.
  5. Turn the element on for one nonprod cluster in its values/clusters/<cluster>.yaml.

Every option of every policy type is in the policy-library README.

items.title: Layout
items.text: Path Contents Chart.yaml Name, description and the policy-library dependency, aliased stack so its schema checks the values templates/policy.yaml One line: {{- include "policy-library.render" . -}} values.yaml Defaults for every setting, under the key described in Element values converters/<name>.yaml The manifest for one configPolicies[].templateNames entry, rendered with Helm's tpl. It reads .Values, and .Parameters (that config policy's templateParameters) when the config policy sets enableTemplateParameters README.md Generated element reference .gitignore Keeps Chart.lock, charts/ and *.tgz out of Git

items.title: Conventions
items.text:
The examples come from stack/metallb. Its values.yaml, trimmed:

stack:
  metallb:
    enabled: false
    toggles:
      quota: false
      addressing: false
    config:
      ipAddressPools: {}
      l2Advertisements: {}
      # bgpAdvertisements, bgpPeers, quota

    policies:
      - name: install
        enabled: true
      - name: config
        enabled: true
        dependencies:
          - name: install
      # quota
      - name: addressing
        enabled: true
        dependencies:
          - name: config

    operatorPolicies:
      metallb:
        enabled: true
        policyRef: install
        upgradeApproval: Automatic
        versions: []
        # namespace, operatorGroup, subscription

    configPolicies:
      - name: metallb-instance
        enabled: true
        policyRef: config
        waitForOperator: metallb
        ignorePending: true
        templateNames:
          - name: metallb-cr
      # resourcequota
      - name: pools
        enabled: true
        policyRef: addressing
        rawTemplate: true
        templateNames:
          - name: metallb-ipaddresspools
      # l2, bgp, peers

Off by default. The element ships with enabled: false. A layer in values/ turns it on for the clusters that need it (Values cascade).

Toggles for optional pieces. The quota and addressing policies ship toggled off, so a cluster turns one on in one line instead of restating the policies list (toggles).

A config map for site data. Converters read addresses, peers and quotas from .Values.stack.metallb.config rather than hard-coding them. Maps merge across the cascade (Merge rules), so a cluster file sets only its own keys. values/clusters/nonprod-west-1.yaml:

stack:
  metallb:
    enabled: true
    toggles:
      addressing: true
    config:
      ipAddressPools:
        services:
          addresses:
            - 10.20.30.100-10.20.30.120
          autoAssign: true
      l2Advertisements:
        services:
          ipAddressPools:
            - services

Install, then configure. The operator and the objects that need its CRDs live in separate policies. config depends on install, and addressing depends on config, so ACM holds each policy Pending until the one before it is compliant. waitForOperator: metallb makes metallb-instance also wait for the operator's CSV, and ignorePending: true keeps that template's Pending state from making its policy noncompliant (policy dependencies, waiting for an operator).

rawTemplate when the object count varies. The pool, advertisement and peer converters range over a config map and emit one object per key, so they set rawTemplate: true. An empty map renders an empty list (raw object templates).

Short names. Element names, policy names and the names of their config and operator policies end up in length-limited object names (Naming limits).

items.title: Good practices
items.text:
• One product per element. Clusters turn an element on as a unit, and its name is in every object name. An operator and its configuration belong together, unrelated settings do not.
  • Put the element name in config and operator policy names. ACM requires template names to be unique across every Policy on a cluster, so two elements that both define an install policy with a ns-monitoring config policy collide. metallb uses metallb-instance. The validator reports collisions as POLICY003.
  • Start in inform. Ship a new policy with remediationAction: inform, roll it out to a nonprod revision, read its compliance, then switch to enforce.
  • Set pruneObjectBehavior only on templates without dependencies, in its own commit. It decides whether removing a policy deletes what it created, and it must reach the cluster before the removal. The validator rejects it on a template with dependencies as POLICY033 (What happens on the managed cluster).
  • Pin operator versions in layers, not in the element. Ship versions: [] and set it per environment or cluster where an unplanned upgrade would hurt (Operator upgrades).
  • Keep secrets out of values. Values live in Git. Read runtime secrets on the hub with an ACM hub template, escaped so Helm passes it through: '{{ "{{" }}hub fromSecret "<namespace>" "<secret>" "<key>" hub{{ "}}" }}' (example). Hub lookups are limited to the policy namespace. To read another, set policies[].hubTemplateOptions.serviceAccountName to a ServiceAccount in the policy namespace that can read it, as acs does. The validator evaluates escaped templates as POLICY081 (ACM templates).
  • Try changes on one cluster first. Push a branch, then pin a nonprod cluster's fleet file to it with a pull request to the default branch (Promoting and rolling back). Keep the branch until the pin moves back. A pin to a deleted branch freezes the Applications of every cluster (Revision).

items.title: Element reference
items.text:
stack/<element>/README.md is generated from the element's values.yaml and its @description and @desc comments, do not edit it by hand. After changing values.yaml, run python tools/doc-generator.py and commit the README, --check reports stale READMEs without writing them. Flags and comment syntax are in tools/README.md.

CI runs the check on pull requests, and the update-docs label regenerates the READMEs on the pull request branch (Documentation Check).

items.title: Global Hub
items.text: How PolicyStack runs when ACM hubs sit under a Multicluster Global Hub.

items.title: What Global Hub does
items.text:
Global Hub is an operator on an ACM hub, the global hub. The ACM hubs it imports are managed hubs. An agent on each managed hub streams that hub's Policies, compliance, events and ManagedClusters through Kafka into PostgreSQL. Grafana dashboards read them there. Global Hub can also move clusters between managed hubs (ManagedClusterMigration, Technology Preview).

It does not push configuration. Global policy distribution was removed in Global Hub 1.7. Delivery stays with GitOps and the global hub's own ACM.

Use Global Hub 1.8.2 (RHSA-2026:68515) or 1.7.3 (RHSA-2026:67842) or later. Earlier releases let one managed hub spoof another hub's compliance data (CVE-2026-71576). Global Hub 1.8 pairs with ACM 2.17, 1.7 with 2.16.

items.title: Import modes
items.text:
The label global-hub.open-cluster-management.io/deploy-mode on a managed hub's ManagedCluster sets how the global hub imports it. Without the label the hub gets no Global Hub agent.

default hosted Managed hub's klusterlet runs On the managed hub On the global hub Managed hub has local-cluster No. Requires disableHubSelfManagement: true Yes Global hub's Policies reach the managed hub Yes No. The webhook turns off the policy and application addons Who reads the managed hub's fleet/hubs/<managed-hub>.yaml The global hub The managed hub Who builds the managed hub's clusters The global hub, on the managed hub (Lifecycle) The managed hub hypershift engine on the managed hub No. Local hosting needs local-cluster Yes When to set the label Any time Before the import. The webhook ignores clusters already imported

Hosted mode also needs the global hub to manage itself, an import kubeconfig that never expires, and network access from the global hub to each managed hub's API. Backup and restore of the managed hub is not supported.

items.title: Layout
items.text:
Install PolicyStack on the global hub and on every managed hub, each with its own hubName (Install PolicyStack). All hubs read the same fleet/. Each hub's ApplicationSets only see the ManagedClusters that hub imports, so a fleet file's Day-2 Applications render on one hub and its lifecycle Application on one hub. For a cluster of a default-mode managed hub these differ: Day-2 renders on the managed hub, lifecycle on the global hub.

fleet/
  hubs/gh.yaml      # the global hub
  hubs/hub-a.yaml   # default-mode managed hub, read by gh
  hubs/hub-b.yaml   # hosted-mode managed hub, read by hub-b
  edge-1.yaml       # hub: hub-a, built by gh on hub-a
  edge-2.yaml       # hub: hub-b, built by hub-b

Default mode only:

  • Set stack.acm.config.selfManaged: false in the managed hub's values. Left at true, the acm element turns local-cluster back on and breaks the import.
  • Do not name a cluster after the hub that manages it. The global hub's Policies for hub-a land in namespace hub-a on hub-a, where a spoke named hub-a would collide.
  • Create fleet/hubs/<hub>.yaml before setting the label. The label is what points the global hub at that file. Without the label it reads fleet/<hub>.yaml, so removing the label deletes the hub's Day-2 Policies (Removing an element).
  • A hub the global hub builds also has fleet/<hub>.yaml, which holds its lifecycle keys. After the import, its version and channel for upgrades go in fleet/hubs/<hub>.yaml.

Hosted mode only: do not create fleet/<managed-hub>.yaml for Day-2. The global hub would render Policies that never reach the hub.

Name each managed hub's ManagedCluster on the global hub after its hubName. Hosted mode finds the hub file and the hub's clusters by hubName, and default mode by the ManagedCluster name, so with one name a mode change moves no file. Global Hub also uses the ManagedCluster name as the hub's identity in its dashboards.

items.title: Lifecycle
items.text:
policystack-lifecycle has two generators (Lifecycle generator):

  1. Fleet files whose hub is this hub's hubName, only when this hub manages itself. Placed on its local-cluster.
  2. Fleet files whose hub is a ManagedCluster of this hub labeled deploy-mode=default. Placed on that managed hub.

A hosted-mode hub and the global hub build their own clusters with the first. A default-mode hub has no local-cluster, renders nothing, and its parent builds for it with the second. ACM delivers the Policies to the managed hub, where every lookup and fromSecret resolves. The credential Secret and the BMC Secret therefore live on the managed hub, as they do in hosted mode.

hypershift is not supported on a default-mode hub. The HyperShift operator is not installed there, so present-lifecycle-<cluster> stays NonCompliant. Use hive or siteconfig, or hosted mode.

Changing a managed hub's mode is a detach and re-import: detach it from the global hub, flip selfManaged, and re-import it with the new label. Its fleet file stays where it is. hive and siteconfig clusters survive and are adopted by the other hub, because no lifecycle Policy sets pruneObjectBehavior and hub stays the same (Abandon). hypershift clusters cannot change mode.

items.title: Do not
items.text:
• Label a PolicyStack hub global-hub.open-cluster-management.io/hub-role. Hub HA copies its ApplicationSets, Applications, Policies and ArgoCD CR to the standby hub.
  • Enable the ACM gitops-addon or Argo CD Agent on a managed hub. They replace openshift-gitops, which runs that hub's PolicyStack.
  • Reuse a cluster name across hubs. fleet/ is shared, and migration needs unique names.
  • Move a cluster that lifecycle builds with ManagedClusterMigration. It moves the ManagedCluster, not its Policies or Applications, and hypershift clusters cannot migrate. Imported clusters migrate cleanly: their fleet file is keyed by name, and the target hub picks it up.

items.title: Installation
items.text: PolicyStack runs on the ACM hub. Everything in install/ is run once per hub; Argo CD reads nothing there. Run the commands from the root of your fork, logged in to the hub as a cluster administrator.

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
• oc, and helm 3.14 or later.
  • On a hub that already runs OpenShift GitOps: its default Argo CD instance, openshift-gitops. The install chart grants its application controller access and the instance runs the ApplicationSets.
  • A fork of PolicyStack. Argo CD reads fleet files and values from it, and upstream ships none. A private fork needs an Argo CD repository secret in openshift-gitops.
  • On a hub that builds clusters from fleet files: ACM 2.16 or later and the rest of Cluster lifecycle prerequisites.

items.title: Install the operators
items.text:
Skip this on a hub that already runs ACM and OpenShift GitOps (Existing hubs).

until helm template install/operators -f stack/acm/values.yaml -f stack/gitops/values.yaml \
      | oc apply -f - && oc get argocd/openshift-gitops -n openshift-gitops; do sleep 30; done
oc wait mch/multiclusterhub -n open-cluster-management --for=jsonpath='{.status.phase}'=Running --timeout=20m
oc wait argocd/openshift-gitops -n openshift-gitops --for=jsonpath='{.status.phase}'=Available --timeout=10m

The install/operators chart renders the Namespace, OperatorGroup and Subscription for each operator, plus the MultiClusterHub, from the acm and gitops element values. They are the objects those elements enforce, so handing the operators over later adopts them in place. The chart installs the channel head and fails on a versions or upgradeApproval pin; pin after handover (Operator upgrades). The loop re-applies until ACM installs the MultiClusterHub CRD and the GitOps operator creates its default Argo CD instance. The MultiClusterHub takes about 10 minutes. A loop that never finishes is a real error, such as an unreachable catalog: stop it and read the oc output.

To override a value, such as stack.acm.config.availabilityConfig: Basic on a single node hub, add -f values/acm/<hub>.yaml.

items.title: Existing hubs
items.text:
The acm and gitops elements adopt an operator only when its namespace, its OperatorGroup name and its Subscription name, which must equal the package, match the element. Check before enabling either element:

oc get subscriptions.operators.coreos.com -A \
  -o custom-columns=NS:.metadata.namespace,NAME:.metadata.name,PACKAGE:.spec.name,CHANNEL:.spec.channel \
  | grep -E 'advanced-cluster-management|openshift-gitops-operator'
oc get operatorgroups -n <NS>
  • NAME differs from PACKAGE: leave that element off. The OperatorPolicy would create a second Subscription.
  • NS differs from the element's, such as GitOps in openshift-operators: set stack.<acm|gitops>.operatorPolicies.<acm|gitops>.namespace and operatorGroup.name to match, or leave that element off. Otherwise OLM gets a second install of the operator.
  • A console-created OperatorGroup, <ns>-xxxxx: set stack.<acm|gitops>.operatorPolicies.<acm|gitops>.operatorGroup.name to it in values/acm/<hub>.yaml.
  • An older channel: set subscription.channel to it, then move one minor at a time.

items.title: Install PolicyStack
items.text:
helm install policystack ./install -n openshift-gitops \
  --set hubName=<hub> --set gitRepo=https://github.com/<org>/<fork>.git \
  --description "$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)"

hubName names the hub's fleet file, fleet/hubs/<hubName>.yaml, and its Applications (The hub). Every hub reading the same repo, including a disaster recovery hub, needs its own. Both values are required and stored in the release, so they are typed only here.

The chart creates:

Object Name Namespace Purpose ApplicationSet policystack, policystack-lifecycle openshift-gitops Applications per element and cluster, and per built cluster (Clusters and Applications) Namespace policy Holds the Policies ManagedClusterSetBinding global openshift-gitops, policy Lets the Placements select every cluster Placement global openshift-gitops Every cluster, tolerating unreachable and unavailable GitOpsCluster argo-acm-importer-global openshift-gitops Creates an Argo CD cluster secret for each cluster the Placement selects ClusterRole, ClusterRoleBinding openshift-gitops-policy-admin Lets the Argo CD application controller manage Policies, PolicySets, Placements and PlacementBindings, the only objects elements render

Every object carries helm.sh/resource-policy: keep, so helm uninstall policystack leaves PolicyStack running. If Helm reports an object that already exists, such as a hand-made global binding, add --take-ownership (Helm 3.18 or later).

Each managed cluster then has an Argo CD cluster secret:

oc get secrets -n openshift-gitops -l argocd.argoproj.io/secret-type=cluster

Next: add a fleet file for the hub and each managed cluster (Onboarding a cluster).

items.title: Hand the operators to PolicyStack
items.text:
Once the stack is proven on the hub, enable the elements in values/acm/<hub>.yaml, and list acm/<hub>.yaml under valueFiles in fleet/hubs/<hub>.yaml (The hub):

stack:
  acm:
    enabled: true
  gitops:
    enabled: true
    toggles:
      instance: false
      link: false

ACM and GitOps upgrades then follow the hub's fleet revision like any other element (Operator upgrades). instance stays off so PolicyStack never reconciles the Argo CD instance that delivers it, and link depends on it. Do not run Install the operators again afterwards: it would reset a channel the hub layer overrides.

items.title: Upgrading
items.text:
Part How Elements, lifecycle, values Merge upstream into the fork, then move fleet revision pins (Rolling out changes) ACM and GitOps Through the elements after handover. Before it, OLM upgrades within the installed channel The install chart helm upgrade, below

The ApplicationSets are not pinned per cluster: a change under install/templates/ reaches every cluster on the hub. Upgrade only when git diff <last>..HEAD -- install/ is not empty, where <last> is the DESCRIPTION of the deployed revision in helm history policystack -n openshift-gitops. After Rollback to <n>, it is revision <n>'s.

helm upgrade policystack ./install -n openshift-gitops --reset-then-reuse-values \
  --description "$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)"

--reset-then-reuse-values takes the new chart defaults and keeps hubName and gitRepo. Roll back with helm rollback policystack <revision> -n openshift-gitops.

items.title: From the appset chart
items.text:
Hubs installed with the old appset release and gitops-prereq/ move over once, with Helm 3.18 or later. First check that the release's stored manifest keeps all four objects; the ApplicationSets gained keep on 2026-10-13. Below 4, run helm upgrade appset once from a commit before install/ existed, with its usual values.

helm get manifest appset -n <ns> | grep -c 'helm.sh/resource-policy'   # 4
helm get values appset -n <ns> -o yaml > appset-values.yaml
helm uninstall appset -n <ns>
helm install policystack ./install -n openshift-gitops --take-ownership -f appset-values.yaml \
  --description "$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)"
oc get applicationset policystack -n openshift-gitops \
  -o jsonpath='{.metadata.annotations.meta\.helm\.sh/release-name}'   # policystack

Reusing the stored values keeps hubName exact; a different one renames and recreates every hub Application. Nothing is deleted. A hub whose ApplicationSet still had preserveResourcesOnDeletion: true gains the resources finalizer on its Applications, and an Application left OutOfSync on a disabled element prunes on its next automated sync.

Then drop the cluster-admin binding the old install step created. Skip this if the openshift-gitops instance also syncs Applications outside PolicyStack, since they may rely on it. Check the new role first, then remove only the cluster-admin binding:

oc auth can-i create policies.policy.open-cluster-management.io -n policy \
  --as=system:serviceaccount:openshift-gitops:openshift-gitops-argocd-application-controller   # yes
oc get clusterrolebinding -o wide | grep 'ClusterRole/cluster-admin' | grep openshift-gitops-argocd-application-controller
oc adm policy remove-cluster-role-from-user cluster-admin -z openshift-gitops-argocd-application-controller \
  -n openshift-gitops --rolebinding-name=<name>

Without --rolebinding-name, the last command edits every cluster-admin binding. Never delete openshift-gitops-policy-admin; nothing recreates it before the next helm upgrade. Afterwards, sync the Applications and check that they stay Synced.

items.title: Teardown
items.text:
oc delete applicationset policystack policystack-lifecycle -n openshift-gitops

This deletes every Application and every Policy they rendered (Removing an element). Every cluster this hub built keeps running, unmanaged (Abandon). Add --cascade=orphan to keep the Applications and Policies.

items.title: Lifecycle reference
items.text: Details behind Cluster lifecycle.

items.title: Install keys
items.text:
Defaults are in lifecycle/values.yaml. values.schema.json rejects unknown keys, and rejects hive or siteconfig keys unless engine selects them.

Shared:

Key Default Notes engine hypershift hypershift, hive or siteconfig. Fixed at create. credential.namespace, credential.name required Hub Secret with pullSecret, ssh-publickey, and for hive the cloud keys. It can live in any namespace. baseDomain "" Required except on KubeVirt, where HyperShift uses the hub's ingress domain. Fixed at create. releaseRepository quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-release The release image is <releaseRepository>:<version>-multi. Point it at a mirror when disconnected. manifests [] Extra hub objects, each with apiVersion, kind and metadata. Created before the cluster, deleted after it.

hypershift:

Key Default Notes platform required KubeVirt, Agent or None. Fixed at create. namespace clusters Namespace of the HostedCluster, its NodePools and the copied secrets. The control plane runs in <namespace>-<cluster>. agentNamespace "" Namespace of the InfraEnv and its Agents. Required on Agent. services APIServer: LoadBalancer; OAuthServer, Konnectivity, Ignition: Route Service name to servicePublishingStrategy. HyperShift requires all four. Fixed at create. hostedCluster {} metadata and spec merged over the generated HostedCluster. spec.release is ignored. nodePools {} Pool name to a NodePool spec merged over the generated one. The NodePool is <cluster>-<pool>.

hive:

Key Default Notes hive.platform required Exactly one of aws, gcp or azure. region is required, plus projectID on GCP and baseDomainResourceGroupName on Azure. Fixed at create. hive.installConfig {} Merged under the generated install-config. Hive drops fields its installer version does not know. hive.clusterDeployment {} metadata and spec merged over the generated ClusterDeployment. spec.provisioning.releaseImage is ignored.

siteconfig:

Key Default Notes siteconfig.templates ai ai (assisted installer) or ibi (image-based install, single node). Fixed at create. siteconfig.templateNamespace open-cluster-management Namespace of the stock <templates>-cluster-templates-v1 and <templates>-node-templates-v1 ConfigMaps. siteconfig.bmcCredential.namespace, .name required Hub Secret with username and password, copied to <cluster>-bmc for every node. siteconfig.clusterInstance {} Merged under the generated ClusterInstance spec. siteconfig.nodes required hostName to its ClusterInstance node. bmcAddress and bootMACAddress are required. Being a map, layers merge per host.

items.title: Generated objects
items.text:
HostedCluster <namespace>/<cluster>: the release image, pullSecret <cluster>-pull-secret, sshKey <cluster>-ssh-key, the platform, services, channel when set, and dns.baseDomain when set. Agent adds platform.agent.agentNamespace. Agent and None add secretEncryption with the generated key <cluster>-etcd-encryption-key. Networking, etcd and everything else are HyperShift's defaults; set them in hostedCluster.spec.

NodePool <namespace>/<cluster>-<pool>: clusterName, the release image, the platform, and management.upgradeType, Replace on KubeVirt and InPlace otherwise. A pool without replicas gets 0.

ClusterDeployment <cluster>/<cluster>: baseDomain, clusterName, the platform with credentialsSecretRef <cluster>-creds, pullSecretRef <cluster>-pull-secret, installConfigSecretRef <cluster>-install-config, the release image, and installAttemptsLimit: 1, so a failed install is not retried. <cluster>-creds holds only the keys Hive reads: aws_access_key_id and aws_secret_access_key, osServiceAccount.json, or osServicePrincipal.json. Then ManagedCluster <cluster> and its KlusterletAddonConfig with every add-on on.

ClusterInstance <cluster>/<cluster>: clusterName, baseDomain, pullSecretRef, sshPublicKey, the templates, clusterImageSetNameRef lifecycle-<cluster>, and per node hostName, bmcCredentialsName <cluster>-bmc and the node templates. bootMode defaults to UEFI, automatedCleaningMode to disabled. ClusterImageSet lifecycle-<cluster> holds the release image. The stock ai KlusterletAddonConfig turns application-manager off, which stops ACM from creating the cluster's Argo CD secret, so the chart suppresses it and renders its own with every add-on on. With -multi, the assisted installer accepts at most 3 control-plane nodes.

Hive and SiteConfig reject changes to the release image, and SiteConfig any spec change until the install completes. The chart reads those fields back from the live objects, so a later version bump or credential rotation never touches them.

items.title: Policy chains
items.text:
present-lifecycle-<cluster> runs these templates in order, each waiting for the one before it to be Compliant:

Template Mode hypershift hive siteconfig present-guard-<cluster> inform NonCompliant if a ManagedCluster with this name exists without the engine's owner annotations (Ownership). Stops the chain. same same present-credentials-<cluster> enforce Namespace install.namespace, <cluster>-pull-secret, <cluster>-ssh-key; on Agent and None the etcd key Namespace <cluster>, <cluster>-pull-secret, <cluster>-creds, <cluster>-install-config Namespace <cluster>, <cluster>-pull-secret, <cluster>-bmc present-manifests-<cluster> enforce install.manifests same same present-cluster-<cluster> enforce HostedCluster, then the NodePools ClusterDeployment, ManagedCluster, KlusterletAddonConfig ClusterImageSet, ClusterInstance, KlusterletAddonConfig present-ready-<cluster> inform The version history shows version Completed and every NodePool reports it spec.installed is true Provisioned is True

absent-lifecycle-<cluster>:

Template Mode hypershift hive siteconfig absent-guard-<cluster> inform Same check as on create same same absent-detach-<cluster> enforce mustnothave Deletes the ManagedCluster while the cluster is up, so its klusterlet is cleaned up same none: SiteConfig would re-create it absent-detached-<cluster> inform mustnothave Waits until the ManagedCluster is gone same none absent-destroy-<cluster> enforce mustnothave Deletes the HostedCluster Deletes the ClusterDeployment; Hive deprovisions with <cluster>-creds Deletes the ClusterInstance; SiteConfig deletes what it rendered absent-destroyed-<cluster> inform mustnothave Waits until the HostedCluster is gone Waits until deprovision finished Waits until the ClusterInstance is gone absent-cleanup-<cluster> enforce Deletes the copied secrets, the etcd key and install.manifests Deletes Namespace <cluster> and install.manifests Deletes Namespace <cluster>, the ClusterImageSet and install.manifests

The credential is never deleted. An enforced delete is Compliant as soon as the API accepts it, so each destroy step is followed by an inform wait. Every template is musthave: fields the operator fills in are not compared, so the Policy does not fight HyperShift, Hive or SiteConfig. Deleting the present Policy deletes nothing, since no lifecycle template sets pruneObjectBehavior.

The etcd key is generated once, while neither it nor the HostedCluster exists. A deleted key is not regenerated, since a new key cannot decrypt etcd: restore it from a backup.

items.title: Day-2 handoff
items.text:
1. hypershift: once the HostedCluster is available, the hypershift-addon creates ManagedCluster <cluster>. hive and siteconfig: once installed, ACM imports the ManagedCluster the chart or SiteConfig created.
  2. The ManagedCluster joins global, the GitOpsCluster creates its Argo CD cluster secret, and ACM adds the clusterID label (Install PolicyStack).
  3. The Day-2 ApplicationSet pairs the secret with the same fleet file and creates the <element>-<cluster> Applications. It ignores hub, state and install.

HyperShift auto-import is on by default. Setting autoImportDisabled in the hypershift-addon-deploy-config AddOnDeploymentConfig leaves a built cluster without Day-2 until it is imported by hand. Labels in hostedCluster.metadata.labels are copied to the ManagedCluster once, when it is created.

items.title: Ownership
items.text:
The guard and detach act only on a ManagedCluster with its engine's owner annotations:

Engine Annotations Set by hypershift open-cluster-management/created-via: hypershift, import.open-cluster-management.io/hosting-cluster-name: <hub ManagedCluster> The hypershift-addon hive lifecycle.policystk.io/hub: <hubName> present-cluster-<cluster> siteconfig lifecycle.policystk.io/hub: <hubName> SiteConfig, from the ClusterInstance's extraAnnotations

A hand-made ManagedCluster needs these annotations, or the guard stops both chains.

items.title: Immutable fields
items.text:
The operators reject changes to these, among others:

  • HostedCluster: services, platform, networking, etcd, issuerURL, controllerAvailabilityPolicy, fips, and dns.baseDomain once set. secretEncryption cannot be removed.
  • NodePool: clusterName, platform.type, arch, management.upgradeType.
  • ClusterDeployment: everything but installAttemptsLimit, powerState, preserveOnDelete and a few others. hive.installConfig changes reach the Secret, not the installed cluster.
  • ClusterInstance: everything until the install completes, then everything but extraAnnotations, extraLabels, suppressedManifests, pruneManifests, and adding a node.

Changing one in the cascade does not change the cluster: present-cluster-<cluster> goes NonCompliant with the API server's message. Revert the value. To change a NodePool's upgradeType or arch, add a new pool and remove the old one. A failed SiteConfig install cannot be fixed in place: set state: absent, then build again with the fix.

items.title: Removing a NodePool or host
items.text:
musthave never deletes, so removing an entry only stops managing it:

  • NodePool: remove the nodePools entry, then oc delete nodepool <cluster>-<pool> -n clusters. A pool from a shared layer, such as workers in platforms/kubevirt.yaml, cannot be removed from a higher layer: scale it to replicas: 0. The schema rejects null.
  • SiteConfig host: remove the nodes entry, then oc edit clusterinstance <cluster> -n <cluster>. Changing a host after install needs the same edit.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text:
Guard refusal. A guard is NonCompliant with "A ManagedCluster with this name was not built by this hub". The cluster was imported, or runs on another hub. Usually hub was added to an imported cluster's fleet file: remove hub, state and install. The guard cannot catch an engine switch before the cluster is imported, so destroy before changing engine.

Render error. A missing version, credential or required key shows on the Application, not the Policy: oc get applications.argoproj.io lifecycle-<cluster> -n openshift-gitops -o jsonpath='{.status.conditions}'.

Missing credential. A Secret that does not exist turns present-credentials-<cluster> NonCompliant with a template error. Without pullSecret the API server rejects the pull secret. Without ssh-publickey no error shows: the cluster gets no SSH key. On hive, a missing cloud key is copied as an empty value and the install fails on the ClusterDeployment.

Hive install failed. present-ready-<cluster> stays NonCompliant and the ClusterDeployment shows ProvisionStopped. Read the installer log, fix the values, destroy and build again. RequirementsMet False with InstallConfigValidationFailed means the install-config and ClusterDeployment regions differ, through hive.clusterDeployment or an edit of hive.platform during the install. Revert it.

Hive deprovision stuck. absent-destroyed-<cluster> stays NonCompliant and the ClusterDeployment shows DeprovisionLaunchError, or its ClusterDeprovision AuthenticationFailure. Fix the keys in <cluster>-creds itself; the absent Policy no longer copies the credential. With HiveConfig deleteProtection: enabled, remove the hive.openshift.io/protected-delete annotation from the ClusterDeployment.

SiteConfig rejected or failed. present-cluster-<cluster> shows a webhook denial, or the ClusterInstance shows Provisioned False. Check oc get clusterinstance <cluster> -n <cluster> -o jsonpath='{.status.conditions}' and the AgentClusterInstall. Destroy, fix, build again. A wrong ref, such as templateNamespace, can also be fixed by creating the missing object.

SiteConfig cluster never imported. The hub cannot resolve api.<cluster>.<baseDomain>. Add the record where the hub resolves it.

SiteConfig deletion paused. The ClusterInstance carries clusterinstance.siteconfig.open-cluster-management.io/paused: a rendered object, usually a BareMetalHost or the ManagedCluster, was not gone within 30 minutes. Fix what holds it, then remove the annotation.

Rebuilding a name. Nothing can be created in Namespace <cluster> while it terminates after a destroy, so the first step that writes there stays NonCompliant with because it is being terminated. Wait for oc get ns <cluster> to return NotFound.

ManagedCluster stuck Terminating. absent-detached-<cluster> stays NonCompliant. Hosted-mode cleanup waits for the guest; ACM skips it once the guest has been unreachable for 5 minutes. Check oc get klusterlet klusterlet-<cluster> -o jsonpath='{.metadata.finalizers}'. If it waits on operator.open-cluster-management.io/klusterlet-hosted-cleanup and the guest will not answer, remove that finalizer.

AgentMachine pre-terminate hook. On Agent, Machines in <namespace>-<cluster> stay Deleting with PreTerminateDeleteHookSucceeded reporting WaitingExternalHook. Remove the hook:

for m in $(oc get machines.cluster.x-k8s.io -n clusters-<cluster> -o name); do
  oc annotate "$m" -n clusters-<cluster> pre-terminate.delete.hook.machine.cluster.x-k8s.io/agentmachine-
done

Agents stuck reclaiming. After a destroy, Agents go to reclaiming while they reboot into discovery. One that cannot ends in UnbindingPendingUserAction: boot it from the discovery ISO by hand. Agents still holding the agent.agent-install.openshift.io/ai-deprovision finalizer block any new cluster that selects them.

items.title: Adding an engine
items.text:
An engine <e> is a component of lifecycle/. templates/policy.yaml renders the component install.engine names, so the ApplicationSet and the fleet keys stay as they are.

  1. Add converters/<e>/: the objects to create, the root object by identity alone for destroy, and its credentials. Read back with lookup every field the engine rejects changes to. End the cleanup converter with include "lifecycle.cleanupManifests".
  2. Add stack.<e> to values.yaml with a present and an absent Policy, following the chains, with no Policy-level remediationAction or pruneObjectBehavior.
  3. Add <e> to the install.engine enum in values.schema.json, with its keys. POLICY090 fails when the enum and the stack components differ (Validation).
  4. Add an owner case to lifecycle.ownerAnnotations, a present and an absent fleet file to tools/validator/testdata/clusters/, and an example to Cluster lifecycle.

An engine that upgrades from the hub maps version onto its objects, as hypershift does. One that only installs uses version at create and leaves upgrades to upgrade (Upgrades).

items.title: Cluster lifecycle
items.text:
Add hub to a cluster's fleet file and that hub builds the cluster. Set state: absent and the hub destroys it. Once ACM imports the cluster, the same fleet file drives its Day-2 configuration like any other cluster (Fleet files).

How it works:

  1. The hub's ApplicationSet policystack-lifecycle creates Application lifecycle-<cluster> for each fleet file that names the hub.
  2. The Application renders the lifecycle/ chart into Policy present-lifecycle-<cluster>, placed on the hub itself. A managed hub imported into a Global Hub in default mode does not manage itself, so its parent renders and places the Policy for it (Global Hub).
  3. ACM governance on the hub creates the cluster's objects one step at a time, each step waiting for the one before it.
  4. When the install finishes, ACM imports the cluster and the Day-2 ApplicationSet takes over. No manual step.

The cluster is built when present-lifecycle-<cluster> is Compliant. Nothing outside ACM and Argo CD runs.

items.title: Pick an engine
items.text:
install.engine picks what builds the cluster. install.platform picks the HyperShift platform.

You want engine Example Upgraded by OpenShift on AWS, GCP or Azure hive AWS, GCP, Azure upgrade on the cluster OpenShift on bare metal with a BMC siteconfig Bare metal upgrade on the cluster Hosted control plane, workers as VMs on the hub hypershift (default), platform: KubeVirt KubeVirt The hub Hosted control plane, bare-metal workers hypershift, platform: Agent Agent The hub Hosted control plane, workers you boot yourself hypershift, platform: None None The hub

A hosted control plane runs as pods on the hub. hive and siteconfig build standalone clusters.

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
On every hub that builds clusters:

  • ACM 2.16 or later.
  • The hub manages itself: its ManagedCluster has the local-cluster label, the default. Or it is a default-mode Global Hub managed hub, and the global hub runs PolicyStack.
  • fleet/hubs/<hubName>.yaml exists for the hub.
  • For hypershift: the hypershift-addon on the hub, on by default. Check with oc get managedclusteraddon hypershift-addon -n local-cluster.
  • A credential Secret on the hub with pullSecret and ssh-publickey, plus the cloud keys for hive. Each example below shows the command. To show it under Infrastructure > Credentials in the console, add the labels cluster.open-cluster-management.io/credentials= and cluster.open-cluster-management.io/type=<type>.

Each example lists what else its engine needs. The fleet files are complete: copy one, change the names and addresses, and merge it. Values shows how to move the common parts into a values layer.

items.title: AWS
items.text:
Needs a public Route 53 zone for baseDomain in the account, and EC2 quota.

oc create namespace hive-credentials
oc create secret generic aws -n hive-credentials \
  --from-literal=aws_access_key_id=<key> --from-literal=aws_secret_access_key=<secret> \
  --from-file=pullSecret=pull-secret.json --from-file=ssh-publickey=id_ed25519.pub

# fleet/ocp-aws.yaml
revision: main
hub: acm-dc1
version: 4.20.8
channel: stable-4.20
install:
  engine: hive
  credential:
    namespace: hive-credentials
    name: aws
  baseDomain: aws.example.com
  hive:
    platform:
      aws:
        region: us-east-2
    installConfig:
      controlPlane:
        name: master
        architecture: amd64
        replicas: 3
        platform:
          aws:
            type: m6i.xlarge
      compute:
        - name: worker
          architecture: amd64
          replicas: 3
          platform:
            aws:
              type: m6i.xlarge

installConfig is any install-config content. The chart sets apiVersion, metadata, baseDomain and platform, Hive adds pullSecret, and sshKey defaults to the credential's. Keep architecture: amd64: without it the install follows the architecture of the hub node it runs on. For single-node OpenShift, set controlPlane.replicas: 1 with type: m6i.2xlarge, and compute[0].replicas: 0.

items.title: GCP
items.text:
Needs a public Cloud DNS zone for baseDomain in the project, a service account with the installer's roles or Owner, and the compute, dns, iam, cloudresourcemanager and serviceusage APIs enabled.

oc create secret generic gcp -n hive-credentials \
  --from-file=osServiceAccount.json=sa-key.json \
  --from-file=pullSecret=pull-secret.json --from-file=ssh-publickey=id_ed25519.pub

# fleet/ocp-gcp.yaml
revision: main
hub: acm-dc1
version: 4.20.8
channel: stable-4.20
install:
  engine: hive
  credential:
    namespace: hive-credentials
    name: gcp
  baseDomain: gcp.example.com
  hive:
    platform:
      gcp:
        projectID: my-project
        region: us-central1
    installConfig:
      controlPlane:
        name: master
        architecture: amd64
        replicas: 3
        platform:
          gcp:
            type: n2-standard-4
      compute:
        - name: worker
          architecture: amd64
          replicas: 3
          platform:
            gcp:
              type: n2-standard-4

items.title: Azure
items.text:
Needs an Azure DNS zone for baseDomain in resource group baseDomainResourceGroupName, and a service principal with Contributor and User Access Administrator on the subscription.

cat > sp.json <<EOF
{"subscriptionId":"<sub>","clientId":"<appId>","clientSecret":"<password>","tenantId":"<tenant>"}
EOF
oc create secret generic azure -n hive-credentials \
  --from-file=osServicePrincipal.json=sp.json \
  --from-file=pullSecret=pull-secret.json --from-file=ssh-publickey=id_ed25519.pub

# fleet/ocp-azure.yaml
revision: main
hub: acm-dc1
version: 4.20.8
channel: stable-4.20
install:
  engine: hive
  credential:
    namespace: hive-credentials
    name: azure
  baseDomain: azure.example.com
  hive:
    platform:
      azure:
        region: eastus
        baseDomainResourceGroupName: dns-rg
    installConfig:
      controlPlane:
        name: master
        architecture: amd64
        replicas: 3
        platform:
          azure:
            type: Standard_D8s_v5
      compute:
        - name: worker
          architecture: amd64
          replicas: 3
          platform:
            azure:
              type: Standard_D4s_v5

items.title: Bare metal
items.text:
Needs:

  • SiteConfig on the hub: stack.acm.config.siteConfig: true in the hub's values layer.
  • Central infrastructure management: an AgentServiceConfig named agent, and the Provisioning provisioning-configuration with watchAllNamespaces: true (plus provisioningNetwork: Disabled on a hub without one). See Enabling central infrastructure management.
  • Hosts with a Redfish BMC that supports virtual media, reachable from the hub. Each host must reach the hub's image service and API.
  • DNS for api.<cluster>.<baseDomain>, resolvable from the hosts and the hub. Multi-node clusters also need api-int and *.apps.
oc create namespace bm-credentials
oc create secret generic hostinventory -n bm-credentials \
  --from-file=pullSecret=pull-secret.json --from-file=ssh-publickey=id_ed25519.pub
oc create secret generic bmc -n bm-credentials --from-literal=username=<user> --from-literal=password=<password>

Single node:

# fleet/sno-edge.yaml
revision: main
hub: acm-dc1
version: 4.20.8
channel: stable-4.20
install:
  engine: siteconfig
  credential:
    namespace: bm-credentials
    name: hostinventory
  baseDomain: edge.example.com
  siteconfig:
    bmcCredential:
      namespace: bm-credentials
      name: bmc
    clusterInstance:
      clusterType: SNO
      networkType: OVNKubernetes
      machineNetwork:
        - cidr: 10.20.30.0/24
    nodes:
      sno-edge.edge.example.com:
        role: master
        bmcAddress: idrac-virtualmedia://10.20.0.11/redfish/v1/Systems/System.Embedded.1
        bootMACAddress: "00:11:22:33:44:55"
        rootDeviceHints:
          deviceName: /dev/sda

Three nodes: set clusterType: HighlyAvailable, add apiVIPs and ingressVIPs, and list each host under nodes:

install:
  siteconfig:
    clusterInstance:
      clusterType: HighlyAvailable
      networkType: OVNKubernetes
      machineNetwork:
        - cidr: 10.20.40.0/24
      apiVIPs: [10.20.40.5]
      ingressVIPs: [10.20.40.6]
    nodes:
      m0.bm-ha.dc1.example.com:
        role: master
        bmcAddress: redfish-virtualmedia://10.20.0.21/redfish/v1/Systems/1
        bootMACAddress: "00:11:22:33:44:01"
      m1.bm-ha.dc1.example.com: ...
      m2.bm-ha.dc1.example.com: ...

Use idrac-virtualmedia:// for Dell and redfish-virtualmedia:// for other vendors. Quote bootMACAddress. clusterInstance takes any ClusterInstance spec field, and each nodes entry any node field.

Image-based install: set siteconfig.templates: ibi. It is single node only, needs the multicluster engine image-based-install-operator component, and the host must be preinstalled with a seed image whose version is version.

items.title: KubeVirt
items.text:
Needs OpenShift Virtualization on the hub, and a LoadBalancer implementation such as MetalLB: the hosted API server is published as a LoadBalancer Service on the hub. The credential may already exist from OpenShift Virtualization setup.

oc create secret generic kubevirt-secret -n open-cluster-management \
  --from-file=pullSecret=pull-secret.json --from-file=ssh-publickey=id_ed25519.pub

# fleet/hcp-kubevirt.yaml
revision: main
hub: acm-dc1
version: 4.20.8
channel: stable-4.20
install:
  platform: KubeVirt
  credential:
    namespace: open-cluster-management
    name: kubevirt-secret
  nodePools:
    workers:
      replicas: 2

baseDomain is optional on KubeVirt: HyperShift uses the hub's ingress domain when it is empty.

items.title: Agent
items.text:
Needs:

  • Central infrastructure management (an AgentServiceConfig), as for bare metal.
  • An InfraEnv in agentNamespace, and hosts booted from its discovery ISO, approved, and labeled to match the NodePool's agentLabelSelector. A pool without a selector claims any free Agent in the namespace.
  • A LoadBalancer implementation on the hub, as for KubeVirt.
  • DNS for *.apps.<cluster>.<baseDomain> pointing at the guest's ingress. values/clusters/hcp-agent.yaml pins it with the metallb element.
oc create namespace hcp-credentials
oc create secret generic hostinventory -n hcp-credentials \
  --from-file=pullSecret=pull-secret.json --from-file=ssh-publickey=id_ed25519.pub

# fleet/hcp-agent.yaml
revision: main
hub: acm-dc1
version: 4.20.8
channel: stable-4.20
install:
  platform: Agent
  credential:
    namespace: hcp-credentials
    name: hostinventory
  baseDomain: dc1.example.com
  agentNamespace: hardware-inventory
  nodePools:
    workers:
      replicas: 2
      platform:
        agent:
          agentLabelSelector:
            matchLabels:
              example.com/cluster: hcp-agent

items.title: None
items.text:
HyperShift creates no machines. You boot each worker with the NodePool's Ignition and approve it. Use this when the workers are VMs or hosts that ACM cannot provision.

Needs the same credential as Agent, a LoadBalancer implementation on the hub, and DNS for *.apps.<cluster>.<baseDomain> pointing at the workers. The guest router listens on the workers' host network, ports 80 and 443.

# fleet/hcp-none.yaml
revision: main
hub: acm-dc1
version: 4.20.8
channel: stable-4.20
install:
  platform: None
  credential:
    namespace: hcp-credentials
    name: hostinventory
  baseDomain: dc1.example.com
  nodePools:
    workers: {}

Once the HostedCluster is up, add a worker:

# Ignition pointer config with the ignition server URL, token and CA
oc get secret -n clusters-hcp-none -o name | grep user-data-hcp-none-workers \
  | xargs oc get -n clusters-hcp-none -o jsonpath='{.data.value}' | base64 -d > worker.ign
# Boot RHCOS with worker.ign as its Ignition or cloud user data, then approve its CSRs twice,
# a minute apart: client, then serving certificate
oc extract secret/hcp-none-admin-kubeconfig -n clusters --to=- > hcp-none.kubeconfig
oc --kubeconfig hcp-none.kubeconfig get csr -o name | xargs oc --kubeconfig hcp-none.kubeconfig adm certificate approve

HyperShift's default service network is 172.31.0.0/16, the AWS default VPC range. On AWS workers set hostedCluster.spec.networking.serviceNetwork to another range at create. A single worker also needs hostedCluster.spec.infrastructureAvailabilityPolicy: SingleReplica.

items.title: Fleet keys
items.text:
Key Default Effect hub none hubName of the hub that builds and owns the cluster (The hub). Without it the cluster is import-only. state present present builds the cluster and keeps it as declared. absent destroys it (Destroy). Requires hub. version none OpenShift release, x.y.z. Required. Bumping it upgrades the cluster (Upgrades). channel none Update channel, such as stable-4.20. Optional. install none What to build. Requires hub. Every key is in the reference.

The cluster name is the fleet file name: a DNS label of at most 30 characters, the most every element fits. The lifecycle chart alone allows 38 (Naming limits). Most install keys are fixed at create (Immutable fields).

items.title: Values
items.text:
The lifecycle Application reads the same cascade as the cluster's Day-2 Applications, lowest precedence first (Order):

  1. lifecycle/values.yaml
  2. values.yaml
  3. Each valueFiles entry, in list order
  4. values/clusters/<cluster>.yaml
  5. hub, state, version, channel and install from the fleet file

Move what clusters share into a layer. These ship with defaults:

Layer Sets values/platforms/aws.yaml engine: hive, credential hive-credentials/aws, a 3+3 m6i.xlarge install-config values/platforms/baremetal.yaml engine: siteconfig, credentials bm-credentials/hostinventory and bm-credentials/bmc, networkType values/platforms/kubevirt.yaml platform: KubeVirt, credential open-cluster-management/kubevirt-secret, 2 workers values/platforms/agent.yaml platform: Agent, credential hcp-credentials/hostinventory, agentNamespace: hardware-inventory

With the AWS layer, the AWS example shrinks to:

# fleet/ocp-aws.yaml
revision: main
hub: acm-dc1
version: 4.20.8
channel: stable-4.20
valueFiles:
  - platforms/aws.yaml
install:
  baseDomain: aws.example.com
  hive:
    platform:
      aws:
        region: us-east-2

Maps merge across layers and lists replace (Merge rules): an installConfig.compute list in the fleet file replaces the layer's whole list. version and channel go only in the fleet file. A shared layer is part of every cluster that reads it, so changing a fixed-at-create key there, such as baseDomain, turns every existing cluster that reads it NonCompliant.

values/clusters/<cluster>.yaml can hold both install for the build and stack for the cluster's elements.

items.title: Watching a build
items.text:
Engine Progress hive oc get clusterdeployment -n <cluster>, and the installer log: oc logs -f -n <cluster> -l hive.openshift.io/install=true -c installer. About 45 minutes on AWS. siteconfig oc get clusterinstance,bmh,agentclusterinstall,agent -n <cluster>. About an hour for single node. hypershift oc get hostedcluster,nodepool -n clusters

For every engine:

oc get policy -n pstack present-lifecycle-<cluster>                 # Compliant = built
oc get configurationpolicy -n local-cluster | grep <cluster>        # each step; -n <managed-hub> in default mode
oc get applications.argoproj.io lifecycle-<cluster> -n openshift-gitops -o jsonpath='{.status.conditions}'   # render errors

Policy chains lists every step.

items.title: Upgrades
items.text:
Bump version in the fleet file, and channel with it on a minor bump (Upgrades).

  • hive and siteconfig clusters upgrade on the cluster through upgrade, like imported ones. The hub keeps the release image the cluster was installed with, since Hive and SiteConfig reject changes to it.
  • hypershift clusters upgrade from the hub. With channel set, the HostedCluster waits until HyperShift lists version in status.version.availableUpdates. Without channel, it moves at once. NodePools follow once the control plane reports the new version Completed. KubeVirt pools replace their VMs; other platforms upgrade nodes in place.

During a hosted upgrade present-lifecycle-<cluster> is NonCompliant, and Compliant again once the control plane and every NodePool report the new version. A minor upgrade that HyperShift blocks because ClusterVersionUpgradeable is False needs the annotation hypershift.openshift.io/force-upgrade-to: <release image> in install.hostedCluster.metadata.annotations.

Clusters install from the -multi release payload, so they are multi-architecture clusters and their updates are too.

items.title: Destroy
items.text:
Set state: absent in the fleet file and merge:

 # fleet/ocp-aws.yaml
 revision: main
 hub: acm-dc1
+state: absent

The hub removes the cluster from ACM, deletes it, waits until it is gone, then deletes the secrets and install.manifests it created. Detaching deletes the cluster's Day-2 Applications and Policies without pruning anything on the cluster. Wait for the Policy, then delete the fleet file and values/clusters/<cluster>.yaml:

oc get policy -n pstack absent-lifecycle-<cluster>

What is left:

Engine After destroy hive Nothing in the cloud account. Hive deprovisions it, usually within 20 minutes. siteconfig The hosts keep running and their disks are not wiped. Power them off or reuse them. hypershift Agent The Agents return to the InfraEnv, free for the next cluster. hypershift None The workers you booted. Delete them, and their DNS.

Deleting the fleet file before the Policy is Compliant abandons the cluster at that step.

items.title: Abandon
items.text:
Deleting the fleet file, or removing its hub key, deletes the Application lifecycle-<cluster> and its Policies. The cluster keeps running, unmanaged. Deleting the ApplicationSets does the same for every cluster the hub built; helm uninstall policystack keeps them (Install PolicyStack).

To re-adopt, restore the file or the key with the same install values.

Moving a cluster to another hub is not supported. Changing hub abandons it on the old hub and builds a second cluster with the same name on the new one. Destroy it on the old hub first.

items.title: Reference
items.text: Lifecycle reference has every install key, the objects each engine creates, the policy chains, ownership, immutable fields, troubleshooting, and how to add an engine.

items.title: Policies
items.text: Elements render their ACM objects with the policy-library chart, its README is the field reference. PolicyStack fixes three inputs. The values key an element reads, the release name every object name builds on, and the selector that targets one cluster.

items.title: Element values
items.text:
An element reads stack.<key>, where <key> is the camelCase form of the chart name in its Chart.yaml. The user-monitoring chart reads stack.userMonitoring. Files in the values cascade use the same keys, so one cluster file configures many elements and each chart reads only its own key. The validator reports a mismatched key as POLICY090.

Every chart also reads the top-level keys policyNamespace, selector and placement. Nothing renders unless stack.<key>.enabled is true.

items.title: Rendered objects
items.text:
Names build on the release, which is the Application name (Applications). In the table, <policy>, <set> and <name> are the name fields of policies[], policySets[] and the template lists, or the key of an operatorPolicies entry. An entry is enabled when its enabled field is true, unless its toggle overrides it.

Object Name Rendered when Policy <policy>-<release> The policy is enabled and at least one enabled template names it in policyRef. ConfigurationPolicy, CertificatePolicy template <policy>-<name> The entry is enabled and the Policy its policyRef names renders. It is embedded in that Policy. OperatorPolicy template <policy>-<name> The entry is enabled and the Policy its policyRef names renders. It adds two ConfigurationPolicy templates: <policy>-<name>-ns for the operator namespace and <policy>-<name>-status, an inform check that the operator's CSV reached Succeeded. PolicySet <set>-<release> The set is enabled and its policies list is not empty. Members resolve to <policy>-<release>. Placement <release> disablePlacements is not true. PlacementBinding <release> disablePlacements is not true and there is a subject to bind. Subjects are the rendered Policies, or the rendered PolicySets when usePolicySetsPlacements is true.

Policies, PolicySets, Placements and PlacementBindings live on the hub in policyNamespace, set to policy in the root values.yaml. The chart ignores policies[].namespace, although its README lists it. Templates have no namespace of their own. They sit inside the Policy's policy-templates, and ACM creates them in the cluster's namespace on the managed cluster.

items.title: Placement
items.text:
The chart turns the injected selector (Injected values) into the Placement's required cluster selector. It holds one expression, on the name label, so each Placement selects only its own cluster. The rendered predicate for nonprod-west-1:

spec:
  predicates:
  - requiredClusterSelector:
      labelSelector:
        matchExpressions:
        - key: name
          operator: In
          values:
            - nonprod-west-1

A top-level placement: key in any cascade file merges into that spec (Placement overview).

An ACM Placement selects only clusters in ManagedClusterSets bound to its namespace. The install chart binds global into policyNamespace (Install PolicyStack).
