The lifecycle/ chart is the exception (Cluster lifecycle). Its Policies build clusters on a hub, so the lifecycle ApplicationSet injects selector, one In expression on the name label for the hub the Policies apply to. The Exists expression on local-cluster in its values.yaml only serves helm lint and the validator (Lifecycle generator). Every lifecycle release lands on the hub, where ACM requires template names to be unique across all Policies, so the chart sets the policy-library option suffixTemplateNames. Its template names are <policy>-<name>-<cluster>, such as present-credentials-hcp-agent.

items.title: Naming limits
items.text:
ACM replicates each Policy into the cluster's namespace on the hub, and names and labels the copy <policyNamespace>.<policy>-<release>. A label value holds at most 63 characters. With policyNamespace: policy, <policy>-<release> gets 56, and the release spends part of that on the element and cluster names. A long element name shrinks the budget of every policy in that element, and a long cluster name that of every policy on that cluster, so keep policy names short.

The lifecycle release is lifecycle-<cluster> and its longest Policy is present, so the replicated name is policy.present-lifecycle-<cluster>: 25 characters plus the cluster name, which leaves the cluster name at most 38. Its longest template, present-credentials-<cluster>, is shorter than 63 for any such name.

Validator rule POLICY001 holds <policyNamespace>.<policy>-<release>, <policyNamespace>.<set>-<release> and every template name (<policy>-<name>) to 63 characters (Rules).

Every element fits a cluster or hub name of up to 30 characters. CI holds new elements to that: POLICY001 checks every policy in each element's values.yaml, enabled or not, against fixture name-budget-30-characters-long. Most elements fit 35 or more.

Worked example: metallb on nonprod-west-1, release metallb-nonprod-west-1. The cluster file turns on the addressing toggle, quota stays toggled off and renders nothing.

Entry Hub Policy Replicated name Characters install install-metallb-nonprod-west-1 policy.install-metallb-nonprod-west-1 37 config config-metallb-nonprod-west-1 policy.config-metallb-nonprod-west-1 36 addressing addressing-metallb-nonprod-west-1 policy.addressing-metallb-nonprod-west-1 40

Templates. the OperatorPolicy install-metallb with its install-metallb-ns and install-metallb-status, then config-metallb-instance, addressing-pools, addressing-l2, addressing-bgp and addressing-peers. The Placement and PlacementBinding are both metallb-nonprod-west-1.

Render it from the repo root. The release name stands in for the Application name and baseline.yaml for the injected selector (Validation).

helm dependency update stack/metallb
helm template metallb-nonprod-west-1 stack/metallb \
  -f values.yaml \
  -f values/environments/nonprod.yaml \
  -f values/datacenters/dc2.yaml \
  -f values/clusters/nonprod-west-1.yaml \
  -f tools/validator/testdata/baseline.yaml

items.title: Library reference
items.text: Chart README: Policy dependencies, Depending on another component, Toggles, Raw object templates, Placement overview.

items.title: Rolling out changes
items.text: A cluster runs what Git holds at the revision its fleet file pins: the element charts, their policy-library pins and every values file. To roll out a change, commit it and point fleet files at a revision that contains it.

items.title: Onboarding a cluster
items.text:
A cluster either already exists and is imported, or a hub builds it from its fleet file. To have a hub build it, add hub, version and install to the fleet file in step 2 and skip step 1: the hub creates the cluster, ACM imports it, and the steps below then apply as written (Cluster lifecycle).

  1. Import the cluster into ACM. The GitOpsCluster then imports it into Argo CD (Install PolicyStack).

  2. Open a pull request to the default branch that adds fleet/<cluster>.yaml, named exactly like the ManagedCluster (Fleet files). The hub's file is fleet/hubs/<hubName>.yaml (The hub).

    # fleet/prod-east-1.yaml
revision: main
valueFiles:
  - environments/prod.yaml
  - datacenters/dc1.yaml
  - platforms/aws.yaml

  3. Add values/clusters/<cluster>.yaml, named exactly like the ManagedCluster, at the revision the fleet file pins. When that is the default branch, add it in the same pull request. It enables the elements this cluster runs beyond what its other layers enable. A misnamed file is skipped without an error (Missing files). The hub's file is values/clusters/<hubName>.yaml (Order).

Import and the pull request can come in either order. Land step 3 before or with step 2: Applications rendered before the cluster's values file exists leave that layer out, which can briefly enable an element the file turns off. Once the cluster is imported and its fleet file is on the default branch, the ApplicationSet creates one Application per element, named <element>-prod-east-1, in openshift-gitops, within about 6 minutes. An element no layer enables syncs with no resources.

oc get applications.argoproj.io -n openshift-gitops | grep prod-east-1

items.title: Promoting and rolling back
items.text:
A cluster pinned to a branch picks up every commit pushed to it. A cluster pinned to a tag or SHA changes only when its fleet file's revision changes. Promote with a pull request that edits revision:

 # fleet/prod-east-1.yaml
-revision: v1.4.0
+revision: v1.5.0
 valueFiles:

The PR's Render Diff comment shows what the new revision changes in the cluster's Policies.

Roll back with git revert of that commit, or with a pull request that sets the previous revision. Both go through the same review as any change to fleet/ (Protection).

Every Application for the cluster switches to the new revision. Application names do not include the revision, so Argo CD updates the same Policies in place. The Placement selector matches only the cluster's name label, so the policies stay bound to the cluster while Argo CD syncs.

An element that exists at the new revision but not the old one gets a new Application. An element missing at the new revision loses its Application and its Policies (Removing an element).

items.title: Disabling an element
items.text:
Set enabled: false under the element's key in a layer that outranks every layer enabling it (Order). values/environments/prod.yaml enables dns, to turn it off on prod-east-1 only, add this to values/clusters/prod-east-1.yaml:

stack:
  dns:
    enabled: false

To turn off one part of an element instead, set its toggle.

Once the change reaches the cluster's revision, the element renders nothing and automated sync prunes its objects from policy, since the ApplicationSet sets allowEmpty. ACM then removes its policies from the managed cluster (What happens on the managed cluster). A failed render prunes nothing: the Application reports a ComparisonError with sync status Unknown, and its Policies stay as they were.

items.title: Removing an element
items.text:
Delete stack/<element>. The Applications carry the resources finalizer, so when a cluster's revision no longer has the directory, the ApplicationSet deletes the element's Application, Argo CD deletes its Policies, PolicySets, Placement and PlacementBinding from policy, and ACM removes the policies from the managed cluster. Clusters pinned to older revisions keep the element until their pin moves.

An Application is also deleted when:

  • The cluster's fleet file is deleted (Offboarding a cluster).
  • The cluster is detached. The GitOpsCluster deletes the cluster's Argo CD secret once its ManagedCluster is gone.
  • The cluster's Argo CD secret, or its clusterID label, disappears for any other reason (Pausing removals).
  • The ApplicationSet is deleted (Teardown).

A fleet file that does not parse, or a revision that does not exist, deletes nothing. The ApplicationSet changes no Application until it is fixed (Revision).

items.title: Offboarding a cluster
items.text:
Delete the cluster's fleet file in a pull request. The ApplicationSet deletes all of its Applications, and with them its Policies (Removing an element).

For a cluster whose fleet file sets hub, the file also decides whether the cluster survives:

  • Destroy. Set state: absent, wait for the Policy absent-lifecycle-<cluster> to be Compliant, then delete the file (Destroy). Detaching deletes the Day-2 Applications and their Policies. The governance add-on is already gone, so nothing is pruned on the cluster.
  • Abandon. Delete the file, or remove hub. The hub deletes the lifecycle Policies and the cluster keeps running, unmanaged (Abandon). Deleting the file also deletes the Day-2 Policies, and templates that set pruneObjectBehavior prune on the still attached cluster.

Do not reuse the cluster's name while its fleet file exists. A cluster imported under that name gets the old file's configuration.

items.title: What happens on the managed cluster
items.text:
Removing a policy from the hub removes it from the managed cluster. What it created there stays unless a ConfigurationPolicy template sets pruneObjectBehavior, which acts only when the template is enforce and the setting reached the managed cluster before the removal:

Case Effect pruneObjectBehavior: None (default) Every object stays. Patched fields keep their values, nothing is reverted. inform Nothing is deleted. DeleteIfCreated Deletes only the objects this ConfigurationPolicy instance created. A recreated policy, or one on a re-imported cluster, adopts the existing objects and does not delete them. DeleteAll Deletes every object the template manages, including ones that existed before the policy. OperatorPolicy The operator, Subscription, CSV, CRDs and CRs stay. A Subscription the policy set to manual approval, because versions is pinned or upgradeApproval is None, stays manual, so upgrades stop. An unpinned Automatic one keeps upgrading, unmanaged. Gatekeeper constraints and constraint templates Deleted. Cluster detached, or governance add-on removed Nothing is pruned. Cluster disconnected Pruning runs when it reconnects.
  • Set pruneObjectBehavior in its own commit, and remove the policy only after that commit reached the managed cluster.
  • Renaming an element, a policy, a template or hubName deletes the old objects and creates new ones. With prune set, that deletes the objects on the managed cluster and creates them again.
  • The validator rejects prune on a template with any dependency: waitForOperator, extraDependencies, the policy's dependencies, or a place after another template or policy under orderManifests or orderPolicies (POLICY033, Validation). ACM deletes a template whenever its dependency is unmet, for example during an operator upgrade, and prune then deletes its objects.
  • Keep the Placement's default tolerations. With placement.tolerations: [], a disconnected cluster drops out of the Placement and loses its policies.

items.title: Pausing removals
items.text:
Before an ACM upgrade or work on the Argo CD cluster secrets, stop the ApplicationSet from deleting Applications. The upgrade to ACM 2.17 can replace a cluster's secret with a renamed one and briefly drop the cluster's Applications, and with them its Policies.

oc patch applicationset policystack -n openshift-gitops --type merge \
  -p '{"spec":{"syncPolicy":{"applicationsSync":"create-update"}}}'

The ApplicationSet still creates and updates Applications, but deletes none. The OpenShift GitOps operator starts the ApplicationSet controller without --policy, so the per-ApplicationSet setting applies. helm upgrade leaves the field in place. Remove it when done:

oc patch applicationset policystack -n openshift-gitops --type json \
  -p '[{"op":"remove","path":"/spec/syncPolicy/applicationsSync"}]'

items.title: Operator upgrades
items.text:
Each operatorPolicies entry renders an OperatorPolicy named after its key (Operator Policy Options, Version pinning). upgradeApproval is None or Automatic. ACM rejects Manual and subscription.installPlanApproval. upgradeApproval and versions decide upgrades:

upgradeApproval versions Effect when enforced Automatic empty The Subscription is set to automatic approval. OLM installs every upgrade the channel offers. Automatic listed The Subscription is set to manual approval. The policy approves an InstallPlan only when the CSV it installs is in versions or equals subscription.startingCSV. None either The policy approves the initial install only, filtered by versions and subscription.startingCSV. It never approves an upgrade, even to a CSV in versions.

An informing policy approves nothing, it reports an installed CSV missing from a non-empty versions as noncompliant.

versions entries are exact CSV names, with no ranges or wildcards. An entry can hold several comma-separated names (ACM 2.14+) or a template (ACM 2.13+).

The hub's own ACM and GitOps follow the same rules once their elements are enabled (Hand the operators to PolicyStack).

Elements ship unpinned, with upgradeApproval: Automatic and versions: []. Pin in a layer. operatorPolicies is a map keyed by entry name, so the layer sets only the fields it changes (Merge rules). To pin metallb on every prod cluster:

# values/environments/prod.yaml
stack:
  metallb:
    operatorPolicies:
      metallb:
        versions:
          - <installed CSV>
        subscription:
          startingCSV: <installed CSV>

oc get csv -n metallb-system on the managed cluster shows the installed CSV. On a cluster that does not have the operator yet, OLM resolves the Subscription to the channel's latest CSV, and the policy does not approve it unless it is listed. startingCSV installs the pinned CSV there instead. Leave it out when the pin is the channel head.

A layer can only override keys the element defines. The validator rejects a new key as POLICY032 (Validation), and the render fails if the key has no policyRef.

When a newer CSV is available, the OperatorPolicy status names it in a message that starts an InstallPlan to update to [<csv>]. OLM picks that CSV from the channel's upgrade graph, the policy only approves or holds it, so a CSV in versions installs only once OLM offers it. Bump in two steps:

  1. Add the new CSV to versions next to the old one. Promote the revision that has it one cluster at a time, by editing each cluster's fleet file (Promoting and rolling back).
  2. Once every cluster runs the new CSV, remove the old one, move startingCSV to the new one, and promote again.

Dropping the old CSV in the same change makes each cluster noncompliant until its upgrade finishes.

To unpin, set versions: [] in a layer that outranks the pin, or delete the pin. To turn an operator off on some clusters, set enabled: false on its key or toggles.<key>: false (Disabling an element). Never set the key to null. Disable the entries that name it in waitForOperator in the same layer, or the render fails. This stops managing the operator but does not uninstall it.

items.title: Upgrades
items.text:
Every cluster upgrades the same way: change version, and channel on a minor bump, in its fleet file and merge.

 # fleet/prod-east-1.yaml
 revision: v3.0.0
-version: 4.20.8
+version: 4.20.12
 channel: stable-4.20
Key Effect version The OpenShift release, x.y.z, the cluster runs. Unset, nothing upgrades the cluster. Required on a cluster a hub builds. channel The update channel. Unset, the cluster's channel is left alone.

Both go only in the fleet file. The validator rejects them in a values layer, so the clusters a merge upgrades are the fleet files it changes, and the render diff shows each one. A wave is one commit that bumps several fleet files. Quote a value YAML reads as a number: unquoted, version: 4.20 is read as 4.2, and the validator rejects it.

items.title: Who upgrades what
items.text:
Cluster Upgraded by Written Built by a hub with the hypershift engine lifecycle-<cluster> on the hub HostedCluster spec.release and spec.channel, then each NodePool's release (Cluster lifecycle) Any other cluster, the hubs included The upgrade element on the cluster ClusterVersion spec.channel, spec.desiredUpdate and spec.upstream

Each field has one writer. upgrade does nothing on a hosted control plane guest, one whose Infrastructure reports controlPlaneTopology: External, since HyperShift owns its ClusterVersion.

items.title: upgrade
items.text:
The element is enabled by default and renders nothing until the fleet file sets version or channel. It renders two Policies, channel-upgrade-<cluster> when channel is set and upgrade-upgrade-<cluster> when version is set:

Template Mode Does channel-pin enforce Sets the ClusterVersion channel. upgrade-guard inform NonCompliant unless version is in availableUpdates, is the desired version, or is at or below the current version. upgrade-trigger enforce Sets desiredUpdate.version once the guard is Compliant, only while version is newer than the current version and no update is progressing. Never image or force. upgrade-progress inform NonCompliant until the cluster has completed version.

A version the cluster's update service does not offer stays held at the guard. Downgrades are never attempted. upgrade-trigger also sets spec.upstream to stack.upgrade.config.upstream, api.openshift.com by default: a cluster on a local OpenShift Update Service sets it in a values layer.

config.targetVersion and config.channel are gone: the render fails while a layer sets them. Move them to the fleet file's version and channel in the commit that bumps revision.

Watch it:

oc get policy -n policy upgrade-upgrade-prod-east-1
oc get clusterversion version -o jsonpath='{.status.history[0]}'   # on the cluster

items.title: Pausing
items.text:
Set the toggle in any layer that the cluster reads, such as values/clusters/<cluster>.yaml:

stack:
  upgrade:
    toggles:
      upgrade: false

This deletes upgrade-upgrade-<cluster>, and an update already started continues on the cluster. channel: false stops managing the channel. A hosted cluster is paused by leaving version where it is.

items.title: Why not ClusterCurator or TALM
items.text: ClusterCurator runs an upgrade as a one-shot Job: a failure is not retried, and a Policy that owns the ClusterCurator cannot tell a finished upgrade from a new one. TALM's ClusterGroupUpgrade is one-shot too and needs its own inform policies. ClusterVersion is declarative, so a Policy can keep enforcing it.

items.title: Validation
items.text:
tools/validator renders every element under stack/ for each fixture cluster in tools/validator/testdata/clusters, building the list of values files the way the ApplicationSet does (Order). It checks the element sources and the rendered output. The fixtures are the example fleet files: prod-east-1.yaml, nonprod-west-1.yaml, the hub's hubs/acm-dc1.yaml, and seven clusters the hub builds: hcp-kubevirt.yaml, hcp-agent.yaml, hive-aws.yaml, sno-edge.yaml, and hcp-retired.yaml, hive-retired.yaml and sno-retired.yaml (state: absent), plus name-budget-30-characters-long.yaml, which holds every element to a 30-character cluster name (Naming limits). A file is named after its cluster, so hubs/acm-dc1.yaml renders as acm-dc1 and reads values/clusters/acm-dc1.yaml. Their files in values/ are rendered too.

For each fixture that sets hub, it also renders the lifecycle/ chart as lifecycle-<cluster>, with the fixture file appended to the cascade in place of the ApplicationSet's valuesObject (Cluster lifecycle).

Helm sees the ACM templates converters escape ({{ "{{" }} ... {{ "}}" }}) only as strings. POLICY081 evaluates them, see ACM templates.

It needs Go and Helm. Use the Helm major version that CI pins (Policy Validate). kubeconform is optional, without it on PATH, POLICY080 is skipped.

items.title: Running it
items.text:
From the repo root, the same commands CI runs, without --github:

make -C tools/validator lint test build
tools/validator/bin/policystack-validator --repo-root . --extra-values tools/validator/testdata/baseline.yaml --include-sample-element --skip POLICY080,POLICY081
for p in tools/validator/testdata/profiles/*.yaml; do
  tools/validator/bin/policystack-validator --repo-root . --only RENDER000,POLICY081 \
    --extra-values "tools/validator/testdata/baseline.yaml,$p"
done

The first checks formatting, vets, tests and builds the validator. The second runs it on the fixtures, the loop evaluates every converter's ACM templates (ACM templates). Policy Validate explains the skips.

baseline.yaml supplies a stand-in selector. One Exists expression on the name label. The chart builds each Placement from selector.matchExpressions, and outside Argo CD nothing injects it, so helm template fails for an enabled element without one. In production the ApplicationSet injects a selector for the one cluster instead (Placement). Files passed with --extra-values take precedence over the whole cascade. They are not applied to lifecycle/, which ships its own selector.

The validator runs helm dependency update on an element unless its charts/ directory already holds <name>-<version>.tgz for every dependency in Chart.yaml, so a policy-library bump fetches the new archive and replaces the stale one.

items.title: Output
items.text:
A clean run prints ok: no findings. Otherwise each finding gives its severity, rule, element (and fixture cluster, for checks on rendered output), and the file to fix, with the line where known:

error POLICY020 [metallb] configPolicies[0] "metallb-instance" references templateNames[0] "metallb-crd" but converters/metallb-crd.yaml does not exist
    at /path/to/policystack/stack/metallb/values.yaml:107:19
error POLICY030 [kiali] policies[0].severity = "hgh", allowed: [low medium high critical]
    at /path/to/policystack/stack/kiali/values.yaml:22:19
warning POLICY021 [metallb] converters/metallb-cr.yaml is not referenced by any templateNames[].name
    at /path/to/policystack/stack/metallb/converters/metallb-cr.yaml:1

2 error(s), 1 warning(s)
Exit code Meaning 0 No errors, warnings alone pass 1 Errors, or warnings with --severity warning 2 The validator itself failed, for example Helm is not on PATH Flag Effect --only Comma-separated rule IDs to run, all others are skipped --skip Comma-separated rule IDs to skip --severity warning Fail on warnings as well as errors --github Write GitHub Actions annotations instead of terminal output --fixtures-dir Fleet files to render instead of the examples, hubs in its hubs/. CI passes fleet when the repo has fleet files --lifecycle-dir The lifecycle chart, default <repo>/lifecycle --render-dir Writes each render to <dir>/<fleet file path without .yaml>/<element>.yaml, a failed one as # RENDER000: lines, nothing for an empty one. Render Diff diffs two of these

--help lists the rest.

items.title: ACM templates
items.text:
POLICY081 resolves each rendered ConfigurationPolicy with go-template-utils, the library ACM uses, in two passes:

  1. {{hub ... hub}} as the policy propagator does. Lookups are limited to the policy namespace unless the policy sets hubTemplateOptions.serviceAccountName.
  2. {{ ... }} as the config-policy-controller does: object-templates-raw whole, each object-templates entry on its own with skipObject.

Both run against an empty cluster. Parsing catches an undefined function in every branch, run or not. A missing object is not reported, because on a real cluster another policy or an operator creates it, and evaluation stops there. So a branch that only runs once objects exist is parsed but not executed.

It fails on:

  • an undefined function or a failed call, such as index on a missing object
  • a hub lookup outside the policy namespace
  • a kind the fake cluster does not serve, which is how a misspelled kind or apiVersion shows. A converter looking up a new kind adds it to kinds in tools/validator/internal/acmtemplates
  • output containing <no value>, or an object without apiVersion or kind

Guard a lookup whose object may not exist yet: dig for nested keys, skipObject in object-templates to skip the object until it does:

href: '{{ "{{" }} $host := (lookup "route.openshift.io/v1" "Route" "ns" "name").spec.host {{ "}}" }}{{ "{{" }} skipObject (not $host) {{ "}}" }}https://{{ "{{" }} $host {{ "}}" }}'

The fixtures leave most elements off, so CI evaluates against tools/validator/testdata/profiles, which turn every element and toggle on. A new element or toggle goes in all-on.yaml, or in variants.yaml if it conflicts with one there. TestProfileCoverage fails until every converter with ACM templates renders under some profile.

The Go tests in tools/validator/internal/acmtemplates also resolve the lifecycle chart's templates against fake hub objects and check the values they produce. A change to a lifecycle converter's ACM template needs a case there.

items.title: Rules
items.text: ID Severity What it catches POLICY001 error Policy/PolicySet ACM-replicated name <ns>.<name>-<release> > 63 chars; ConfigurationPolicy/OperatorPolicy/CertificatePolicy metadata.name (<parent>-<sub>) > 63 chars POLICY002 error Duplicate rendered metadata.name WITHIN one element POLICY003 error Two different elements render a policy-template with the same name. ACM requires template names to be unique across every Policy on a cluster, so policies[].name: install + configPolicies[].name: ns-monitoring in two elements is rejected on-cluster with "Template name must be unique". Covers toggled-off entries and the -ns/-status templates an operatorPolicy generates POLICY010 error policyRef points to nonexistent or disabled parent policy POLICY011 error dependency reference that can never be satisfied: unknown dependencies/extraDependencies target, unknown element:, element: on a template kind, waitForOperator naming no enabled operator, or a target policy policy-library never emits (no enabled sub-policy attached) POLICY020 error templateNames[].name has no matching converters/<name>.yaml; <name> may contain /, as in hypershift/ready POLICY021 warning Converter file not referenced by any templateNames[].name POLICY030 error/warning Invalid enum: severity / remediationAction / complianceType / upgradeApproval (None or Automatic). In operatorPolicies entries also: subscription.installPlanApproval set, a versions entry or subscription.startingCSV that is not a valid CSV name (templated entries skipped, comma-separated versions entries split), and a name: key, which is ignored (warning) POLICY031 error/warning values keys policy-library never reads: enable: (element renders nothing) and defaultPolicy: (metadata silently dropped) are errors; default.severity/.remediationAction/.disabled are warnings. Also flags rawTemplate: true with more than one templateNames entry, and operatorPolicies as a list (policy-library 3.x needs a map) POLICY032 error/warning stack.<el>.operatorPolicies in a values layer: a key the element's values.yaml does not define, a list, or any POLICY030 operator problem. Reported once per layer file POLICY033 error/warning configPolicies[].pruneObjectBehavior other than None: an invalid value, an effective remediationAction other than enforce (a policy-level value overrides the template's), or any dependency (waitForOperator, extraDependencies, parent dependencies, orderManifests unless first template, orderPolicies unless first Policy), since ACM deletes the template whenever the dependency is unmet. DeleteAll is a warning POLICY034 error Top-level version or channel in a values layer: only the fleet file sets them. Reported once per layer file POLICY040 error policySets[].policies[] references a name not in policies[] POLICY050 error Invalid fleet file: YAML error, unknown key, missing or empty revision, revision, hub, state, version, channel or valueFiles entry Argo CD reads as a number or boolean, valueFiles entry that is null, listed twice, or not a file under values/; version that is not x.y.z, install.version; empty hub, version or channel, hub with no hubs/<hub>.yaml, hub naming the cluster itself, hub in a hub file, state other than present/absent, install that is not a map, state or install without hub, or a cluster that sets hub whose name is not a DNS label POLICY060 warning policy-library version drift across element Chart.yaml files POLICY070 error helm lint non-zero POLICY080 error kubeconform schema check on rendered manifests POLICY081 error An escaped ACM template ACM would fail to resolve, resolved hub then managed on an empty cluster: an undefined function in any branch, a failed call such as index on nil, a hub lookup outside the policy namespace without hubTemplateOptions.serviceAccountName, a kind discovery does not serve, or output with <no value> or an object without apiVersion/kind. A missing object is not a failure. Findings name the sub-policy without its cluster suffix and carry no cluster, so a broken template reports once POLICY090 error Chart.yaml name → camelCase mismatch with single key under stack:. For a chart whose values.schema.json has an install.engine enum (lifecycle/), a stack: key that is not an engine or an engine with no stack: key. Every other check then runs on each engine's component, and each fixture renders the one its install.engine selects POLICY091 error An element name equal to another's, or starting with another's followed by -. Release names join element and cluster with -, so a on cluster b-c and a-b on cluster c would share one Application and its Policies. lifecycle/ takes part, which reserves lifecycle RENDER000 error helm template failed

items.title: Values cascade
items.text: Every Application renders its element chart with an ordered list of values files. The cluster's fleet file chooses the files, and later files override earlier ones. The ApplicationSet builds the list in the templatePatch of appset.yaml.

items.title: Order
items.text:
Lowest precedence first. Paths are relative to stack/<element>, the Application's source path.

  1. values.yaml: the element defaults.
  2. ../../values.yaml: the repo root, shared by every element. It sets policyNamespace.
  3. ../../values/<entry>, one per entry in the valueFiles list of the cluster's fleet file, in list order. Nothing sorts the list, so a later entry overrides an earlier one.
  4. ../../values/clusters/<name>.yaml, where <name> is the ManagedCluster name, or hubName on the hub (The hub).
  5. valuesObject, the keys the ApplicationSet injects. Argo CD ranks it above every values file.

A lifecycle Application reads the same files with paths relative to lifecycle/: values.yaml, ../values.yaml, ../values/<entry>, ../values/clusters/<cluster>.yaml. Its valuesObject holds the fleet file's hub, state, version, channel and install (Values). Elements ignore the top-level install key and only lifecycle/ reads it, so one cluster file can hold both install and stack.

items.title: Missing files
items.text:
The ApplicationSet sets ignoreMissingValueFiles: true, so Argo CD skips any listed file that does not exist at the cluster's revision. A cluster needs a file in values/clusters/ only where it changes something.

The same setting hides mistakes. Each of these drops a layer without an error, and the Application syncs from the remaining files:

  • A typo in a valueFiles entry.
  • A valueFiles entry added on the default branch for a file that the cluster's pinned revision does not have yet.
  • A cluster file whose name differs from the ManagedCluster name.

The validator reports a valueFiles entry that is not a file under values/ (POLICY050, Validation). It checks the tree it runs on, not each cluster's revision, so it does not catch the other two.

Elements default to off, so a dropped layer usually shows up as an element that never turns on. Compare the Application's value files with the repo at the cluster's revision:

oc get applications.argoproj.io infra-nodes-prod-east-1 -n openshift-gitops \
  -o jsonpath='{.spec.source.helm.valueFiles}'

items.title: Merge rules
items.text:
Helm merges the files in order.

  • Maps merge key by key. A later file sets only the keys it changes: nonprod-west-1.yaml sets retention and storage under stack.userMonitoring.config.prometheus, and the element defaults supply the rest.
  • Lists replace. A later list overwrites the whole earlier list: dc2.yaml restates the element's default registries next to its mirror.

An element's policies and configPolicies are lists, so a layer cannot change one entry without restating them all. It flips an entry through the toggles map instead, and settings go in the config map that the element's converters read (Conventions). operatorPolicies is a map keyed by entry name, so a layer sets one field of one entry, such as stack.metallb.operatorPolicies.metallb.versions. versions itself is a list and replaces (Operator upgrades).

items.title: Schema
items.text:
Each element aliases its policy-library dependency as stack, so Helm checks the merged stack key against the library's values.schema.json. The check runs after every layer and valuesObject merge. An unknown key or a wrong type then fails the render instead of producing a different policy:

Error: values don't meet the specifications of the schema(s) in the following chart(s):
stack:
- at '/certManager': additional properties 'enabeld' not allowed

Argo CD reports a failed render as a ComparisonError and does not sync or prune. Every element validates the whole stack key, so a typo under one element in a shared layer fails every Application that reads that layer. The schema does not check:

  • top-level keys, such as policyNamespace or selector;
  • element names under stack, so stack.certManagr is still ignored;
  • anything inside config, templateParameters or the selectors.

Never set skipSchemaValidation on the ApplicationSet.

items.title: Layout
items.text:
stack/<element>/values.yaml    element defaults
values.yaml                    shared by every element: policyNamespace
values/
├── environments/   nonprod.yaml  prod.yaml
├── datacenters/    dc1.yaml  dc2.yaml
├── platforms/      agent.yaml  aws.yaml  baremetal.yaml  kubevirt.yaml  vmware.yaml
├── tenants/        payments.yaml
├── acm/            acm-dc1.yaml
└── clusters/       acm-dc1.yaml  aws-prod.yaml  hcp-agent.yaml  nonprod-west-1.yaml  prod-east-1.yaml

items.title: Example files
items.text:
The files under values/ configure the example clusters. They are a starting point, not a complete configuration. Every element but upgrade ships with enabled: false, and the layer that should run an element turns it on. upgrade acts only on the fleet file's version and channel (Upgrades). The Read by column names the example fleet files that list the file, or the cluster whose name matches it.

File Read by Holds values/environments/prod.yaml prod-east-1, hubs/acm-dc1, hcp-agent, sno-edge, sno-retired The security and compliance baseline for every prod cluster: cert-manager, External Secrets, the Compliance Operator, manual remediations and cluster DNS values/environments/nonprod.yaml nonprod-west-1, hcp-kubevirt, hcp-retired, hive-aws, hive-retired Placeholder, sets nothing values/datacenters/dc1.yaml prod-east-1, hubs/acm-dc1, hcp-agent, sno-edge, sno-retired install.baseDomain for clusters built in dc1. Turns no element on values/datacenters/dc2.yaml nonprod-west-1 Site facts only: the registry allowlist through the dc2 mirror. Turns no element on values/platforms/aws.yaml prod-east-1, hive-aws, hive-retired Toggles for the node elements: clone the worker MachineSet. install: engine hive, the credential and the install-config machine pools values/platforms/vmware.yaml No example Toggles for the node elements: clone each worker MachineSet, one per vSphere failure domain values/platforms/baremetal.yaml hubs/acm-dc1, sno-edge, sno-retired Toggles for the node elements: no infra MachineSets, and storage nodes are existing nodes labeled in place. install: engine siteconfig, the credentials and networkType values/platforms/kubevirt.yaml hcp-kubevirt, hcp-retired install only: platform KubeVirt, the credential and a workers NodePool of 2 values/platforms/agent.yaml hcp-agent install only: platform Agent, the Agent namespace and the credential. No default NodePool values/tenants/payments.yaml No example A custom layer: the GitOps operator without its instance, plus a payments team Argo CD values/acm/acm-dc1.yaml hubs/acm-dc1 Reserved for the hub's own ACM and GitOps elements. Left commented out so PolicyStack does not reconcile its own delivery path (Hand the operators to PolicyStack) values/clusters/acm-dc1.yaml The hub, hubName: acm-dc1 The hub's elements, and a commented list of the elements left off and why values/clusters/prod-east-1.yaml ManagedCluster prod-east-1 Infra nodes, machine health checks and user workload monitoring. Its fleet file pins the update channel values/clusters/hcp-agent.yaml lifecycle-hcp-agent and ManagedCluster hcp-agent install: configure services. stack: the guest's MetalLB ingress pool values/clusters/nonprod-west-1.yaml ManagedCluster nonprod-west-1 Enforces the dc2 registry allowlist, the cluster's own MetalLB address pool, and user workload monitoring values/clusters/aws-prod.yaml ManagedCluster aws-prod Values for an AWS test cluster: the OpenShift Data Foundation to Loki storage chain and additional operator installs. Rename it to the target ManagedCluster name before use, its header lists the fleet file it expects

CI renders every element with the files the example fleet files in tools/validator/testdata/clusters/ list (Validation). None of them lists vmware.yaml or payments.yaml, and no example cluster is named aws-prod, so CI reads those files only when a fleet file in fleet/ uses them.

items.title: Worked example
items.text:
fleet/prod-east-1.yaml lists the files for prod-east-1:

revision: main
valueFiles:
  - environments/prod.yaml
  - datacenters/dc1.yaml
  - platforms/aws.yaml

For the infra-nodes element, the ApplicationSet creates the Application infra-nodes-prod-east-1 with these files:

valueFiles:
  - values.yaml
  - ../../values.yaml
  - ../../values/environments/prod.yaml
  - ../../values/datacenters/dc1.yaml
  - ../../values/platforms/aws.yaml
  - ../../values/clusters/prod-east-1.yaml

The environment and datacenter files set nothing for this element. The merged stack.infraNodes, trimmed:

enabled: true                 # clusters/prod-east-1.yaml
toggles:
  mcp: true                   # element default
  config: true                # element default
  aws: true                   # platforms/aws.yaml
  vmware: false               # platforms/aws.yaml
  ready: true                 # element default
  workloads: false            # element default
  restore: false              # element default
config:
  replicas: 1                 # clusters/prod-east-1.yaml
  zones:                      # clusters/prod-east-1.yaml, replaces the default []
    - us-east-1a
    - us-east-1b
    - us-east-1c
  instanceType: m6i.2xlarge   # clusters/prod-east-1.yaml
  # every other config key keeps its element default

valuesObject then adds the one-cluster selector, selectedName and selectedId.

The dc1 hub carries ACM's local-cluster label, so it reads fleet/hubs/<hubName>.yaml (The hub). With hubName: acm-dc1, fleet/hubs/acm-dc1.yaml:

revision: main
valueFiles:
  - environments/prod.yaml
  - datacenters/dc1.yaml
  - platforms/baremetal.yaml
  - acm/acm-dc1.yaml

For nfd, the Application is nfd-acm-dc1:

valueFiles:
  - values.yaml
  - ../../values.yaml
  - ../../values/environments/prod.yaml
  - ../../values/datacenters/dc1.yaml
  - ../../values/platforms/baremetal.yaml
  - ../../values/acm/acm-dc1.yaml
  - ../../values/clusters/acm-dc1.yaml

values/clusters/acm-dc1.yaml turns the element on. On the hub, hubName takes the place of the ManagedCluster name, local-cluster, in the Application name and the cluster file, so values/clusters/local-cluster.yaml is never read.

items.title: CI Workflows
items.text:
The GitHub Actions workflows live in .github/workflows/. The checks run on pull requests and on pushes to main. Update Documentation fixes stale element READMEs on request. Render Diff comments on pull requests.

Workflow Runs on Fails when Policy Validate (validate.yml) Changes to stack/, lifecycle/, install/, tools/sample-element/, values/, values.yaml, fleet/, tools/validator/ Validator tests fail, the validator reports an error, the install charts check fails, or a fleet file's revision does not resolve to a commit with stack/, plus lifecycle/converters/hypershift/ for a file that sets hub and an upgrade element that reads version for a file that sets version or channel Documentation Check (docs-check.yml) Changes to stack/, the doc generator or its tests Generator tests fail or a stack/<element>/README.md is out of date Render Diff (render-diff.yml) PRs to the default branch changing stack/, lifecycle/, values/, values.yaml or fleet/, in a repo with fleet files Not a gate. Fails only when the validator does not build Update Documentation (docs-update.yml) update-docs label added to a PR Not a gate, it fixes what Documentation Check reports Documentation Site (docs-site.yml) Every PR and push to main The strict build finds a relative .md link or anchor that does not resolve, or a missing snippet

The checks also run from the Actions tab (workflow_dispatch). A newer push to the same PR cancels the run in progress.

items.title: Policy Validate
items.text:
1. Checks gofmt, vets and builds tools/validator (make -C tools/validator lint build) with the Go version from tools/validator/go.mod.
  2. Runs the validator against the fixture clusters with --github and --include-sample-element, so tools/sample-element/ stays valid. Each finding is annotated on the PR diff at the file and line to fix. Errors fail the job, warnings are annotated only.
  3. Runs it again with --only RENDER000,POLICY081 for each profile in tools/validator/testdata/profiles, which turn every element on, so every converter's ACM templates are evaluated (ACM templates). A finding both profiles report is annotated once. This step runs even when step 2 fails, so the PR shows its annotations too.
  4. If fleet/*.yaml or fleet/hubs/*.yaml exist, runs the validator again with --fixtures-dir fleet, so a fork checks its fleet files. It renders the PR's stack/ and values/ for each file, not the tree at the file's revision; Render Diff renders each at its revision. Upstream ships no fleet files and skips this step.
  5. Checks every fleet file's revision. It must be a tag, a branch or a commit SHA of 5 to 40 hex characters, the forms Argo CD resolves, and point at a commit that contains stack/. A file that sets hub also needs lifecycle/converters/hypershift/, and one that sets version or channel an upgrade element that reads them; older revisions ignore both keys. A pin to the PR's base branch is checked against the merge commit. Each failure is annotated on the fleet file. The checkout fetches full history (fetch-depth: 0) so tags and branches resolve.
  6. Checks the install charts, which nothing else renders: helm lint install, hubName and gitRepo fail an install when empty, policyNamespace in install/values.yaml equals the root values.yaml, and install/operators renders two Subscriptions and a MultiClusterHub from the acm and gitops element values (Installation). Runs even when an earlier step fails.
  7. Runs the validator's tests (make -C tools/validator test), last so a failing test does not hide the annotations.

The pin check catches typos and pins like gh-pages. It cannot catch a branch deleted after the merge, which fails generation for every cluster. See Revision.

Helm is pinned by HELM_VERSION in the workflow. Keep it on the major the hub's Argo CD uses. POLICY080 is skipped. The chart emits only Policy, PolicySet, Placement and PlacementBinding, and the rule skips those kinds, so it would check nothing. Step 2 skips POLICY081, which step 3 runs on every converter. The fleet step keeps it.

To reproduce locally, see Validation.

items.title: Render Diff
items.text:
Comments on the PR with what the merge changes in each real cluster's rendered Policies. Only clusters in fleet/ count: a repo without fleet files, or a PR that changes no cluster's render, gets no comment.

### Fleet render: 3 cluster(s) change

> [!WARNING]
> `edge-3` pins `v1.4`, which is not a tag, branch or commit. Merging stops Argo CD from generating Applications for every cluster until it is fixed.

| Cluster | Revision | Changes |
|---|---|---|
| `prod-east-1` | `main` | user-monitoring: 1 Policy changed |
| `nonprod-west-1` | `v1.0.0` → `main` | metallb: **render failed** |
| `edge-2` | new at `main` | 6 elements, 21 objects added |

Below the table, each cluster has a collapsed block with the diff of each changed element, or the Helm error of a failed render. Changes count rendered objects by kind and name. An element that failed on the base branch and renders now shows render fixed, one that fails the same way on both sides shows nothing. A cluster added or removed gets a total and no diff.

A fleet file whose revision does not resolve, or whose tree the validator cannot load, is a warning above the table instead of a row.

How it works, in .github/scripts/render-diff.sh:

  1. Reads the fleet files on the base branch (before) and in the PR merge commit (after).
  2. Resolves each revision like the pin check: tag, branch, then SHA. The default branch or HEAD means the base tip before and the merge commit after, so a cluster pinned to main shows the PR and a cluster pinned to a tag changes only when its pin moves. A cluster with the same file and commit on both sides is skipped.
  3. Renders each remaining fleet file in a worktree at its commit with policystack-validator --only RENDER000 --render-dir.
  4. Compares the two sides per element and posts the comment, edited on every push and deleted when nothing changes.

The comment stops at about 60,000 characters, under GitHub's 65,536 limit. The full patch is the render-diff.patch artifact of the run.

PRs from forks and Dependabot get a read-only token, so they get the result in the job summary instead. The job that holds the write token runs no code from the PR.

Placements carry the Exists selector from tools/validator/testdata/baseline.yaml, standing in for the one the ApplicationSet injects. Both sides get the same one, so it never shows as a change.

Every rendered commit gets a fresh worktree and runs helm dependency update for each chart. Expect about half a minute per distinct commit.

items.title: Documentation Check
items.text:
1. Runs the doc generator tests (python -m unittest tools/test_doc_generator.py).
  2. Runs python tools/doc-generator.py --check, which regenerates every element README in memory and compares it with stack/<element>/README.md, ignoring the Generated: timestamp.

If an element README is stale, the Verify Documentation check fails with an annotation saying how to fix it:

  • run python tools/doc-generator.py and commit stack/*/README.md, or
  • add the update-docs label to the PR.

items.title: Update Documentation
items.text:
Runs when the update-docs label is added to a PR from a branch in this repository.

  1. Regenerates stack/*/README.md from the PR branch, skipping READMEs that differ only in the Generated: timestamp.
  2. If anything changed, commits it as github-actions[bot] with the message docs: update documentation [auto-generated] and pushes to the PR branch.
  3. A push made with GITHUB_TOKEN does not start workflows, so it dispatches Documentation Check and Policy Validate on the branch to check the new commit.
  4. Removes the label.

PRs from forks are skipped. Their token is read-only. Run the generator locally instead.

items.title: Documentation Site
items.text:
Builds this site from docs/ with zensical build --strict. PRs only build.

On main, a separate job publishes the build. It pushes site/ plus .nojekyll to the gh-pages branch as a single commit, authenticated as a GitHub App. Pages serves the site from the root of gh-pages (Settings > Pages > Deploy from a branch).

Only that App can change gh-pages. GITHUB_TOKEN cannot be a ruleset bypass actor, and its pushes do not start a Pages build. One-time setup:

Where Setting Org Settings > GitHub Apps An App with no webhook and only Contents: Read and write, installed on this repository only Settings > Environments > gh-pages-publish Deployment branches: main only. Variable DOCS_APP_CLIENT_ID, secret DOCS_APP_PRIVATE_KEY Settings > Rules > Rulesets Branch ruleset on gh-pages: Restrict creations, Restrict updates, Restrict deletions, Block force pushes. Bypass list: the App only, Always allow

Keep all four rules in that ruleset: every publish force-pushes, and the App bypasses only the rules of rulesets that list it. Leave the github-pages environment as it is; the Pages build runs from gh-pages.

The site is unversioned and built from main. For a cluster pinned to an older revision, read docs/ at that revision on GitHub.

To build locally, run from the repo root, where snippet paths resolve:

pip install -r tools/requirements-docs.txt
zensical serve            # live preview
zensical build --strict   # the CI check

serve does not watch the validator README, restart it after editing the rules table. Strict mode does not check absolute links, nav entries in zensical.toml, or content included through snippets. Keep the rules section of tools/validator/README.md free of relative links.

items.title: Dependencies
items.text: Actions are pinned to commit SHAs, with the version in a trailing comment. Dependabot (.github/dependabot.yml) opens weekly PRs for the actions, the validator's Go modules and the Python pins in tools/requirements.txt and tools/requirements-docs.txt (the same /tools pip entry). The Helm version in validate.yml is not covered and is updated by hand.
